title: Simplicity of zeta zeros
open: Is every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function simple? Equivalently, prove that each zero of \(\zeta(s)\) with real part between 0 and 1 has multiplicity one — a statement about multiplicity, logically separate from whether the zeros lie on the critical line.
status: The question has been studied since the early days of zeta theory. It is known that a positive proportion of the zeros are simple, but neither simplicity of every zero nor an unconditional density-one theorem has been proved.
solved_when: It is shown that no nontrivial zero of \(\zeta(s)\) has multiplicity greater than one.
why: Multiple zeros alter the error terms in the explicit formulas linking zeros to primes, and the presence or absence of multiplicities distinguishes the conjectural models of prime fluctuations.
key_works: Hugh Montgomery (1973), *The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function*, [DOI:10.1090/pspum/024/9944](https://doi.org/10.1090/pspum/024/9944); Kyle Pratt, Nicolas Robles, Alexandru Zaharescu and Dirk Zeindler (2020), *More than five-twelfths of the zeros of ζ are on the critical line*, [arXiv:1802.10521](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.10521).

title: Montgomery pair correlation
open: Do the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function, after local rescaling, exhibit the pair-correlation density conjectured by Montgomery? Formally, show that the pair correlation of distinct rescaled zeros agrees with the predicted density.
status: The conjecture was made in 1973. Montgomery proved it for a restricted Fourier-support range assuming the Riemann Hypothesis; the unrestricted correlations remain open. Key works: Hugh Montgomery (1973), *The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1090/pspum/024/9944); [Montgomery's research page](https://public.websites.umich.edu/~hlm/pc.html).
solved_when: The pair-correlation density of distinct, locally rescaled zeta zeros is established (unconditionally, or at least without the restricted Fourier-support limitation).
why: A solution would connect fine-scale fluctuations of the primes to the local eigenvalue statistics of random Hermitian matrices.
key_works: Hugh Montgomery (1973), *The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1090/pspum/024/9944); [Montgomery’s research page](https://public.websites.umich.edu/~hlm/pc.html).

title: Lindelöf hypothesis
open: Does the Riemann zeta function on the critical line grow slower than any fixed power of \(t\)? That is, prove \(\zeta(1/2+it)=O_\varepsilon((1+|t|)^\varepsilon)\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
status: Proposed in 1908. Subconvexity gives positive power bounds; Bourgain's published exponent \(13/84+\varepsilon\) is a major benchmark. RH implies Lindelöf, but the converse is unknown.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the bound \(\zeta(1/2+it)=O_\varepsilon((1+|t|)^\varepsilon)\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
why: It would provide nearly optimal cancellation estimates underlying divisor problems, short sums, and moment calculations.
key_works: Jean Bourgain (2017), *Decoupling, exponential sums and the Riemann zeta function*, [arXiv:1408.5794](https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.5794), [DOI:10.1090/jams/860](https://doi.org/10.1090/jams/860).

title: Binary Goldbach conjecture
open: Is every even integer greater than two the sum of two primes?
status: The problem originates in Goldbach’s 1742 correspondence with Euler. Chen’s theorem permits one summand to have at most two prime factors, and exhaustive verification by Tomás Oliveira e Silva, Siegfried Herzog and Silvio Pardi (2014), *Empirical verification of the even Goldbach conjecture and computation of prime gaps up to \(4\cdot10^{18}\)* ([author record](https://sweet.ua.pt/tos/bib/4.12.html), [DOI:10.1090/S0025-5718-2013-02787-1](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0025-5718-2013-02787-1)), reaches \(4\times10^{18}\).
solved_when: A proof that each even integer \(n > 2\) admits a representation \(n = p + q\) with \(p, q\) both prime.
why: It would settle a basic universal additive representation problem for primes and breach a longstanding sieve obstruction.
key_works: Tomás Oliveira e Silva, Siegfried Herzog and Silvio Pardi (2014), *Empirical verification of the even Goldbach conjecture and computation of prime gaps up to \(4\cdot10^{18}\)*, [author record](https://sweet.ua.pt/tos/bib/4.12.html), [DOI:10.1090/S0025-5718-2013-02787-1](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0025-5718-2013-02787-1).
aliases: Strong Goldbach conjecture; even Goldbach conjecture.

title: Twin prime conjecture
open: Are there infinitely many primes \(p\) such that \(p+2\) is also prime? Equivalently, prove that the prime pairs \((p, p+2)\) occur infinitely often.
status: The conjecture is classical and explicitly associated with de Polignac's 1849 conjectures. Bounded-gap methods establish infinitely many consecutive-prime gaps at most 246, but they do not force gap two; see D. H. J. Polymath (2014), *Variants of the Selberg sieve, and bounded intervals containing many primes*, [arXiv:1407.4897](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.4897), [DOI:10.1186/s40687-014-0012-7](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40687-014-0012-7).
solved_when: A proof that infinitely many primes \(p\) have \(p+2\) prime is given.
why: It would establish a fixed prime-pair pattern beyond the reach of current parity-limited sieve methods, whose limitations are the central obstruction.
key_works: D. H. J. Polymath (2014), *Variants of the Selberg sieve, and bounded intervals containing many primes*, [arXiv:1407.4897](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.4897), [DOI:10.1186/s40687-014-0012-7](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40687-014-0012-7).

title: Infinitely many primes of the form \(n^2+1\)
open: Are there infinitely many positive integers \(n\) for which \(n^2+1\) is prime? In other words, does the irreducible quadratic polynomial \(n^2+1\) take prime values infinitely often?
status: One of Landau’s four problems highlighted in 1912. Iwaniec proved in 1978 that infinitely many values have at most two prime factors, counted with multiplicity (Henryk Iwaniec (1978), *Almost-primes represented by quadratic polynomials*, [DOI:10.1007/BF01578070](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01578070)).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that \(n^2+1\) is prime for infinitely many positive integers \(n\).
why: A fundamental test of prime-producing irreducible polynomials in one variable; resolving it would mark a decisive advance in understanding primes in sparse polynomial sequences.
key_works: Henryk Iwaniec (1978), *Almost-primes represented by quadratic polynomials*, [DOI:10.1007/BF01578070](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01578070).

title: Legendre’s conjecture
open: Is there always a prime strictly between two consecutive perfect squares? Formally, prove that for every integer \(n\ge1\) the interval \(n^2<p<(n+1)^2\) contains a prime.
status: The conjecture is usually dated to 1798 and remains open. The best result toward it, the Baker–Harman–Pintz theorem (Roger Baker, Glyn Harman and János Pintz (2001), *The Difference Between Consecutive Primes, II*, [DOI:10.1112/plms/83.3.532](https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/83.3.532)), guarantees primes in sufficiently large intervals of length \(x^{0.525}\), which does not reach the required square-root scale.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every interval \(n^2<p<(n+1)^2\), for integer \(n\ge1\), contains a prime; equivalently, shortening the known prime-containing interval length from \(x^{0.525}\) down to the required square-root scale.
why: It isolates the core difficulty of obtaining uniform prime existence in short intervals, beyond what current sieve and analytic methods achieve.
key_works: Roger Baker, Glyn Harman and János Pintz (2001), *The Difference Between Consecutive Primes, II*, [DOI:10.1112/plms/83.3.532](https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/83.3.532).

title: Cramér’s prime-gap upper bound
open: Is the gap between consecutive primes always bounded by a constant multiple of the square of the logarithm? Formally, prove or disprove \(p_{n+1}-p_n=O((\log p_n)^2)\) — a constant-factor bound that stops short of asserting Cramér's disputed exact limiting constant.
status: Proposed in 1936, the problem remains open. Unconditional uniform bounds on prime gaps remain polynomial in \(p_n\), and refined random-prime models — such as those of Andrew Granville (1995), *Harald Cramér and the distribution of prime numbers*, [DOI:10.1080/03461238.1995.10413946](https://doi.org/10.1080/03461238.1995.10413946) — change the predicted constants without proving the logarithmic-square bound.
solved_when: An unconditional proof (or disproof) of \(p_{n+1}-p_n=O((\log p_n)^2)\) for all \(n\).
why: It would determine the order of magnitude of the largest local deserts among the primes.
key_works: Andrew Granville (1995), *Harald Cramér and the distribution of prime numbers*, [DOI:10.1080/03461238.1995.10413946](https://doi.org/10.1080/03461238.1995.10413946); Baker, Harman and Pintz (2001), *The Difference Between Consecutive Primes, II*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/83.3.532).

title: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture
open: Can one prove that the primes are equidistributed in arithmetic progressions up to moduli as large as \(x^\theta\) for every fixed \(\theta<1\)? Formally, that for each fixed \(\theta<1\), the summed maximal discrepancy over moduli \(q\le x^\theta\) is \(O_A(x/(\log x)^A)\) for every \(A>0\).
status: Formulated in 1968 by Elliott and Halberstam. The Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem supplies level of distribution \(1/2\); all known results beyond that level impose restrictions on moduli, residue classes, or averaging. Related work: P. D. T. A. Elliott and Heini Halberstam (1968), *A conjecture in prime number theory* (bibliographic details verify); D. H. J. Polymath (2014), *Variants of the Selberg sieve, and bounded intervals containing many primes*, [arXiv:1407.4897](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.4897).
solved_when: For every fixed \(\theta<1\) and every \(A>0\), the summed maximal discrepancy of primes across residue classes modulo \(q\) over all moduli \(q\le x^\theta\) is \(O_A(x/(\log x)^A)\).
why: It would strengthen prime-pattern sieves and uniformity estimates for primes across arithmetic progressions, powering results on prime constellations and gaps currently out of reach at the Bombieri–Vinogradov level.
key_works: P. D. T. A. Elliott and Heini Halberstam (1968), *A conjecture in prime number theory* (bibliographic details verify); D. H. J. Polymath (2014), *Variants of the Selberg sieve, and bounded intervals containing many primes*, [arXiv:1407.4897](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.4897).

title: Chowla’s Liouville correlation conjecture
open: Does the Liouville function behave like a random sign along every fixed pattern of shifts? Formally, prove that for every fixed set of distinct nonnegative integers \(h_1,\ldots,h_k\), the correlations of the Liouville function at these shifts average to zero.
status: The conjecture originates in Chowla's 1965 program. The logarithmically averaged two-point and odd-order versions are established — Terence Tao (2016), *The logarithmically averaged Chowla and Elliott conjectures for two-point correlations*, [arXiv:1509.05422](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05422), and Tao and Joni Teräväinen (2017), *Odd order cases of the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture*, [arXiv:1710.02112](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.02112). The ordinary two-point average remains open, including shifts zero and one.
solved_when: For every fixed set of distinct nonnegative integers \(h_1,\ldots,h_k\), the correlation average of the Liouville function \(\lambda\) over those shifts tends to zero as the averaging range grows.
why: A proof would give a precise meaning to randomness in the parity of prime factorization, settling the expected complete independence of the Liouville function's signs.
key_works: Terence Tao (2016), *The logarithmically averaged Chowla and Elliott conjectures for two-point correlations*, [arXiv:1509.05422](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05422); Tao and Joni Teräväinen (2017), *Odd order cases of the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture*, [arXiv:1710.02112](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.02112).

title: Artin’s primitive root conjecture
open: Is every integer \(a\ne-1\) that is not a perfect square a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes? A complete proof should also confirm the predicted positive density of such primes, including the known correction factors.
status: The conjecture was proposed in 1927. Hooley proved it in 1967 under suitable GRH assumptions; an unconditional proof remains unknown even for \(a=2\). A survey of the problem is given in Pieter Moree (2012), *Artin's Primitive Root Conjecture—A Survey*, [DOI:10.1515/integers-2012-0043](https://doi.org/10.1515/integers-2012-0043).
solved_when: For each integer \(a\ne-1\) that is not a perfect square, it is proved unconditionally that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes, with the conjectured positive density and correction factors.
why: It explains when a single integer generates the multiplicative group of a prime field, which underlies the deterministic construction of primitive roots used in computational number theory and cryptography.
key_works: Pieter Moree (2012), *Artin’s Primitive Root Conjecture—A Survey*, [DOI:10.1515/integers-2012-0043](https://doi.org/10.1515/integers-2012-0043).

title: Existence of odd perfect numbers
open: Does any odd positive integer equal the sum of its proper positive divisors? Equivalently, does an odd perfect number exist?
status: The problem has ancient roots. Ochem's maintained computation reports that a hypothetical example exceeds \(10^{2200}\) and has at least 115 prime factors counted with multiplicity; the peer-reviewed 2012 benchmark was \(10^{1500}\) (Pascal Ochem and Michaël Rao (2012), *Odd perfect numbers are greater than \(10^{1500}\)*, [DOI:10.1090/S0025-5718-2012-02563-4](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0025-5718-2012-02563-4); Ochem, [maintained project](https://www.lirmm.fr/~ochem/opn/)).
solved_when: An odd perfect number is exhibited, or it is proved that none exists.
why: Would settle whether the classical classification of even perfect numbers exhausts all possibilities.
key_works: Pascal Ochem and Michaël Rao (2012), *Odd perfect numbers are greater than \(10^{1500}\)*, [DOI:10.1090/S0025-5718-2012-02563-4](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0025-5718-2012-02563-4); Ochem, [maintained project](https://www.lirmm.fr/~ochem/opn/).

title: Lehmer’s totient problem
open: Can a composite number \(n\) have Euler's totient function divide \(n-1\), that is, \(\varphi(n)\mid n-1\)? Equivalently, does this divisibility condition characterize the primes?
status: Asked in 1932. Any composite example must be odd, square-free, and satisfy severe size and prime-factor restrictions; these do not eliminate every possibility.
solved_when: A proof that no composite \(n\) satisfies \(\varphi(n)\mid n-1\), or an explicit composite example that does.
why: A proof would give a purely divisibility-based characterization of the primes; an example would upend that characterization.
key_works: D. H. Lehmer (1932), *On Euler’s totient function* (bibliographic details verify); S. D. Cohen and P. Hagis Jr. (1980), *On the number of prime factors of n if φ(n) divides n−1* (identifier verify); [Formal Conjectures source issue](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/issues/90).

title: Carmichael’s totient multiplicity conjecture
open: Does Euler's totient function never take any value exactly once — that is, whenever \(\varphi(n)=m\), is there always another positive integer \(n'\ne n\) with \(\varphi(n')=m\)?
status: The conjecture dates to 1907. Kevin Ford (1998), *The distribution of totients* ([announcement](https://www.ford126.web.illinois.edu/wwwpapers/totients-era.pdf); revised treatment, [arXiv:1104.3264](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3264)), gives enormous necessary lower bounds for a counterexample and settles other multiplicity questions, but does not exclude multiplicity one.
solved_when: For every positive integer \(n\) with \(\varphi(n)=m\), some \(n'\ne n\) is exhibited or proven to exist with \(\varphi(n')=m\); equivalently, a counterexample \(m\) with a unique totient preimage is shown to exist.
why: A positive answer would reveal universal redundancy in the inverse Euler-totient problem, showing no totient value ever has a unique solution.
key_works: Kevin Ford (1998), *The distribution of totients*, [announcement](https://www.ford126.web.illinois.edu/wwwpapers/totients-era.pdf); revised treatment, [arXiv:1104.3264](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3264).

title: Irrationality of Euler’s constant
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Is Euler's constant irrational? Formally, determine whether the limit γ of the difference between the harmonic series and the natural logarithm is a rational number.
status: Euler introduced the constant in the eighteenth century. Explicit approximants and equivalent criteria exist, but none decides irrationality. See Jeffrey C. Lagarias (2013), *Euler's constant: Euler's work and modern developments*, [arXiv:1303.1856](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.1856), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0273-0979-2013-01423-X).
solved_when: A proof that γ is irrational, or a proof that it is rational, is produced.
why: It would extend irrationality methods beyond the families of constants accessible to current logarithmic and hypergeometric techniques.
key_works: Jeffrey C. Lagarias (2013), *Euler’s constant: Euler’s work and modern developments*, [arXiv:1303.1856](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.1856), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0273-0979-2013-01423-X).

title: Irrationality of \(\zeta(7)\)
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Is the value of the Riemann zeta function at the odd integer 7, namely \(\zeta(7)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-7}\), irrational? This is a concrete instance of the odd-zeta problem, where individual odd zeta values remain out of reach.
status: Part of the longstanding odd-zeta problem. It is known that infinitely many odd zeta values are irrational, but this does not identify any particular value. The September 2026 result establishing irrationality of \(\zeta(5)\) does not automatically extend to seven. Key works: Tanguy Rivoal (2000), *La fonction zêta de Riemann prend une infinité de valeurs irrationnelles aux entiers impairs*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0764-4442(00)01624-4); Frank Calegari (2026), *zeta(5) is irrational*, [exposition](https://galoisrepresentations.org/2026/09/24/zeta5-is-irrational/).
solved_when: A proof that \(\zeta(7)\) is irrational is given.
why: It would push explicit irrationality results beyond the special values currently under control, advancing the broader odd-zeta program.
key_works: Tanguy Rivoal (2000), *La fonction zêta de Riemann prend une infinité de valeurs irrationnelles aux entiers impairs*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0764-4442(00)01624-4); Frank Calegari (2026), *zeta(5) is irrational*, [exposition](https://galoisrepresentations.org/2026/09/24/zeta5-is-irrational/).

title: Algebraic independence of \(e\) and \(\pi\)
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Are \(e\) and \(\pi\) algebraically independent — that is, is there no nonzero polynomial \(P\in\mathbb Q[X,Y]\) with \(P(e,\pi)=0\)? No relation of any algebraic kind between these two constants is currently known to be impossible.
status: Both constants have individually been known to be transcendental since the nineteenth century, but their joint algebraic independence remains open; even the irrationality of each of \(e+\pi\) and \(e\pi\) separately is unproved. Key work: Michel Waldschmidt (2004), *Open Diophantine Problems*, [arXiv:math/0312440](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0312440).
solved_when: A proof that no nonzero polynomial \(P\in\mathbb Q[X,Y]\) satisfies \(P(e,\pi)=0\).
why: It would establish genuine independence between the two most familiar transcendental constants, showing their transcendence is not merely parallel but algebraically unrelated.

title: Littlewood’s conjecture
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Is it true that every pair of real numbers can be simultaneously approximated multiplicatively by integers, in the sense that \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\|n\alpha\|\|n\beta\|=0\) for all real \(\alpha,\beta\), where \(\|x\|\) denotes distance to the nearest integer?
status: Proposed around 1930. Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss proved that the exceptional set has Hausdorff dimension zero; eliminating every exceptional pair remains open. See Manfred Einsiedler, Anatole Katok and Elon Lindenstrauss (2006), *Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood’s conjecture*, [manuscript](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~einsiedl/EKLslnr.pdf).
solved_when: The liminf above is shown to equal zero for every pair \((\alpha,\beta)\) of real numbers — equivalently, the exceptional set is shown to be empty.
why: It would resolve a fundamental simultaneous multiplicative Diophantine approximation problem, showing that multiplicative approximation is always possible for pairs of reals.
key_works: Manfred Einsiedler, Anatole Katok and Elon Lindenstrauss (2006), *Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood’s conjecture*, [manuscript](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~einsiedl/EKLslnr.pdf).

title: Zaremba’s conjecture
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Is there an absolute constant \(A\) such that every positive integer \(q\) is the denominator of some reduced fraction \(a/q\) whose finite continued-fraction expansion has all partial quotients bounded by \(A\)? The classical proposed value is \(A=5\).
status: The conjecture was formulated in 1971. Jean Bourgain and Alex Kontorovich (2014), *On Zaremba’s conjecture*, [arXiv:1107.3776](https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.3776), [Annals article](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2014/180-1/p03), established a density-one result with an absolute bound; covering every denominator remains beyond current results.
solved_when: An absolute constant \(A\) (ideally \(A=5\)) is exhibited and proved to work for every positive denominator \(q\).
why: A solution would provide rational approximations with uniformly bounded partial quotients at every prescribed denominator, giving fine uniform control in Diophantine approximation.
key_works: Jean Bourgain and Alex Kontorovich (2014), *On Zaremba’s conjecture*, [arXiv:1107.3776](https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.3776), [Annals article](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2014/180-1/p03).

title: Unbounded partial quotients of the cube root of two
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Are the partial quotients in the ordinary continued-fraction expansion of the cube root of two unbounded? Equivalently, is no constant \(C\) such that every partial quotient of \(\sqrt[3]{2}\) is at most \(C\)?
status: This is a classical instance of a nineteenth-century problem. Roth's theorem restricts exceptionally accurate rational approximation to algebraic numbers, but it does not decide boundedness of the partial quotients. Background appears in Yann Bugeaud (2012), *Distribution Modulo One and Diophantine Approximation*, [DOI:10.1017/CBO9781139017732](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139017732).
solved_when: A proof that the partial quotients of \(\sqrt[3]{2}\) are unbounded, or a disproof showing they are bounded.
why: It would reveal the qualitative continued-fraction behavior of an explicit algebraic number of degree greater than two, where almost nothing is currently known.
key_works: Yann Bugeaud (2012), *Distribution Modulo One and Diophantine Approximation*, [DOI:10.1017/CBO9781139017732](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139017732).

title: Markov-number uniqueness conjecture
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: If positive integers \(x\le y\le z\) satisfy \(x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz\), does the largest coordinate \(z\) uniquely determine the pair \(x,y\)?
status: Formulated by Frobenius in 1913. Numerous restricted cases, including important prime-power cases, are known; the full Markov tree remains unresolved. Key reference: Martin Aigner (2013), *Markov's Theorem and 100 Years of the Uniqueness Conjecture*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-319-00888-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-00888-2).
solved_when: For every Markov triple \((x,y,z)\) with \(x\le y\le z\), no other Markov triple has the same value of \(z\).
why: It would settle whether the largest coordinate uniquely encodes a classical Diophantine configuration, a question driving a century of work on the Markov tree.
key_works: Martin Aigner (2013), *Markov’s Theorem and 100 Years of the Uniqueness Conjecture*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-319-00888-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-00888-2).
aliases: Frobenius uniqueness conjecture; Markoff uniqueness conjecture.

title: abc conjecture
open: For every \(\varepsilon>0\), prove that coprime positive integers \(a+b=c\) satisfy
status: Formulated by Masser and Oesterlé in 1985. Mochizuki's claimed proof was published in 2021, but objections from Scholze–Stix (Peter Scholze and Jakob Stix (2018), *Why abc is still a conjecture*, [manuscript](https://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/scholze/WhyABCisStillaConjecture.pdf); Shinichi Mochizuki (2021), *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-Volume Computations and Set-Theoretic Foundations*, [publication](https://ems.press/journals/prims/articles/201528)) remain unresolved in the wider community; this records a proof controversy rather than an uncontested theorem.
solved_when: A proof of the conjecture — for every \(\varepsilon>0\), a bound of the conjectured form holds for all coprime positive integers \(a+b=c\) — is accepted by the community as an uncontested theorem.
why: A solution would impose sweeping restrictions on integer equations and on the interaction between addition and prime factorization, yielding consequences across arithmetic geometry.
key_works: Peter Scholze and Jakob Stix (2018), *Why abc is still a conjecture*, [manuscript](https://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/scholze/WhyABCisStillaConjecture.pdf); Shinichi Mochizuki (2021), *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-Volume Computations and Set-Theoretic Foundations*, [publication](https://ems.press/journals/prims/articles/201528).

title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
open: Does the arithmetic of an elliptic curve over a number field determine its analytic behavior? Specifically, is the Mordell–Weil rank of every elliptic curve over a number field equal to the order of vanishing of its \(L\)-function at \(s=1\), and does the leading coefficient of that \(L\)-function at \(s=1\) satisfy the predicted formula?
status: The conjecture was developed in the 1960s. Over \(\mathbb Q\), major rank and finiteness theorems are known for analytic ranks zero and one; arbitrary ranks and the full leading-term formula remain open. Andrew Wiles (2006), *The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture*, in *The Millennium Prize Problems*; [Clay statement and references](https://www.claymath.org/millennium/birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture/). A US$1,000,000 Clay Millennium Prize, subject to the institute's rules, is attached to its resolution.
solved_when: For every elliptic curve over a number field, one proves that the order of vanishing of its \(L\)-function at \(s=1\) equals its Mordell–Weil rank and proves the predicted leading-coefficient formula.
why: It would connect rational solutions of cubic equations to analytic information encoded in their \(L\)-functions, bridging the algebraic and analytic sides of the curve.
key_works: Andrew Wiles (2006), *The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture*, in *The Millennium Prize Problems*; [Clay statement and references](https://www.claymath.org/millennium/birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture/).
prize: US$1,000,000 Clay Millennium Prize, subject to the institute’s rules.

solved.paper: The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for elliptic curves over Q

title: Finiteness of Tate–Shafarevich groups
open: Is the Tate–Shafarevich group \(\operatorname{Sha}(A/K)\) finite for every abelian variety \(A\) over a number field \(K\)? That is, can the obstruction to the local-to-global principle for principal homogeneous spaces under \(A\) ever be infinite?
status: The problem emerged in the 1950s–1960s. Euler-system methods establish important elliptic-curve cases, including analytic rank at most one over \(\mathbb{Q}\); unrestricted rank remains open. Background appears in M. L. Brown (2025), *Shafarevich-Tate Groups*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-71893-9](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-71893-9), and Bjorn Poonen (2025), *The origins of the Tate conjecture*, [slides](https://math.mit.edu/~poonen/slides/tate2025.pdf).
solved_when: Finiteness of \(\operatorname{Sha}(A/K)\) is proved for every abelian variety over every number field.
why: A solution would fully control the failure of the local-to-global principle for principal homogeneous spaces, making the arithmetic of abelian varieties computable through their Mordell–Weil groups and local data.
key_works: M. L. Brown (2025), *Shafarevich-Tate Groups*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-71893-9](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-71893-9); Bjorn Poonen (2025), *The origins of the Tate conjecture*, [slides](https://math.mit.edu/~poonen/slides/tate2025.pdf).

title: Uniform bound for rational points on curves
open: Is there a uniform cap on how many rational points a curve of given genus can have over a fixed number field? Formally: for each number field \(K\) and each genus \(g\ge2\), prove there exists a constant \(B(K,g)\) such that \(\#C(K)\le B(K,g)\) for every smooth projective curve \(C\) of genus \(g\) over \(K\).
status: A central uniformity question since the 1980s–1990s. Faltings proves curve-by-curve finiteness; Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger give bounds incorporating the Mordell–Weil rank. Key works: Vesselin Dimitrov, Ziyang Gao and Philipp Habegger (2021), *Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves*, [arXiv:2001.10276](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.10276); Patricia Pacelli (1997), *Uniform boundedness for rational points*, [arXiv:alg-geom/9601004](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9601004).
solved_when: For every number field \(K\) and every \(g\ge2\), a constant \(B(K,g)\) is proven that bounds \(\#C(K)\) uniformly over all smooth projective genus-\(g\) curves over \(K\).
why: It would turn Faltings's individual curve-by-curve finiteness into a uniform structural constraint on families of curves, giving arithmetic geometry a quantitative handle on rational points across all curves of a given genus.
key_works: Vesselin Dimitrov, Ziyang Gao and Philipp Habegger (2021), *Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves*, [arXiv:2001.10276](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.10276); Patricia Pacelli (1997), *Uniform boundedness for rational points*, [arXiv:alg-geom/9601004](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9601004).

title: Effective Mordell conjecture
open: Is there an unconditional algorithm that, given equations for a smooth projective curve of genus at least two over a number field, outputs all of its rational points and certifies that the list is complete?
status: Faltings proved finiteness in 1983 without a general effective bound. Chabauty, descent, and other methods cover extensive families; García-Fritz–Pasten's 2025 work *Effective Mordell for curves with enough automorphisms* ([arXiv:2503.10443](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10443)) adds effective cases.
solved_when: An algorithm exists that, for any smooth projective curve \(C/K\) of genus at least two, terminates and returns all \(K\)-rational points together with a proof of completeness.
why: It would turn Faltings' finiteness theorem into a universally terminating rational-point computation, making the full set of solutions effectively computable rather than merely known to be finite.
key_works: Natalia García-Fritz and Hector Pasten (2025), *Effective Mordell for curves with enough automorphisms*, [arXiv:2503.10443](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10443).

title: Vojta’s height inequality
open: For a smooth projective variety over a number field, together with a normal-crossings divisor, an ample divisor, a finite set of places, and an ε>0, does Vojta's conjectural height inequality always hold? Formally: prove that the height inequality relating h_K(D), h_A, the proximity function, and the height h(x) holds for all integral points outside a Zariski-closed exceptional subset.
status: Conjectured by Paul Vojta (1987), *Diophantine Approximations and Value Distribution Theory*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/BFb0072989). Roth's theorem and several subspace-theorem results are known to be special cases; the general inequality remains open. See also Vojta (2010), *Diophantine Approximation and Nevanlinna Theory*, [manuscript](https://math.berkeley.edu/~vojta/cime/cime.pdf).
solved_when: The height inequality is proven in the stated generality — for every smooth projective X/K, normal-crossings divisor D, ample divisor A, finite set of places S, and ε>0 — with only the conjectured Zariski-closed exceptional subset permitted.
why: A proof would unify major Diophantine approximation and rational-point conjectures into a single framework.
key_works: Paul Vojta (1987), *Diophantine Approximations and Value Distribution Theory*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/BFb0072989); Vojta (2010), *Diophantine Approximation and Nevanlinna Theory*, [manuscript](https://math.berkeley.edu/~vojta/cime/cime.pdf).

title: Potential density on K3 surfaces
open: Does every K3 surface over a number field acquire a Zariski-dense set of rational points after passing to some finite field extension?
status: A longstanding open problem. Density is known for substantial classes of K3 surfaces admitting elliptic fibrations or sufficiently many automorphisms, notably in Fedor Bogomolov and Yuri Tschinkel (2000), *Density of rational points on elliptic K3 surfaces*, [arXiv:math/9902092](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9902092); see also Brendan Hassett, *Potential density of rational points*, [lecture abstract](https://www.math.columbia.edu/~thaddeus/seattle/abstracts/hassett2.html).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given for arbitrary K3 surfaces over number fields: either every such surface becomes Zariski-dense in rational points over a finite extension of its base field, or an explicit counterexample is exhibited.
why: It is a key test case for arithmetic predictions on varieties with trivial canonical class, sitting between rationally connected varieties and general type.
key_works: Fedor Bogomolov and Yuri Tschinkel (2000), *Density of rational points on elliptic K3 surfaces*, [arXiv:math/9902092](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9902092); Brendan Hassett, *Potential density of rational points*, [lecture abstract](https://www.math.columbia.edu/~thaddeus/seattle/abstracts/hassett2.html).

title: Modularity of elliptic curves over number fields
open: Is every elliptic curve over an arbitrary number field modular — that is, does it correspond to a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb A_K)\) whose local \(L\)-factors match those of the curve?
status: The framework dates to the 1950s–1970s. All elliptic curves over \(\mathbb Q\) are modular, with major extensions over totally real fields; arbitrary number fields remain open. A recent overview is Jack A. Thorne (2023), *Elliptic curves and modularity*, [DOI:10.4171/8ECM/12](https://doi.org/10.4171/8ECM/12), [publisher chapter](https://ems.press/books/standalone/262/5175).
solved_when: Every elliptic curve over any number field \(K\) is shown to admit an attached cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb A_K)\) with matching local \(L\)-factors.
why: It would extend analytic tools and automorphic structure throughout the arithmetic of elliptic curves — placing \(L\)-functions, analytic ranks, and related invariants on automorphic footing for curves over arbitrary number fields.
key_works: Jack A. Thorne (2023), *Elliptic curves and modularity*, [DOI:10.4171/8ECM/12](https://doi.org/10.4171/8ECM/12), [publisher chapter](https://ems.press/books/standalone/262/5175).

title: Fontaine–Mazur conjecture
open: Which p-adic Galois representations of a number field actually come from geometry? Formally, show that every irreducible p-adic Galois representation of a number field, unramified outside finitely many places and de Rham above p, comes up to Tate twist from étale cohomology of an algebraic variety.
status: The conjecture was formulated in 1995. Modularity-lifting results settle many two-dimensional cases under hypotheses, while arbitrary dimensions remain open. Key works: Jean-Marc Fontaine and Barry Mazur (1995), *Geometric Galois representations* (identifier verify); Ramla Abdellatif, Supriya Pisolkar, Marine Rougnant and Lara Thomas (2022), *From Fontaine-Mazur conjecture to analytic pro-p groups—a survey*, [arXiv:2205.03558](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03558).
solved_when: Every irreducible p-adic Galois representation of a number field that is unramified outside finitely many places and de Rham above p is shown, up to Tate twist, to arise from the étale cohomology of an algebraic variety.
why: A proof would characterize precisely which arithmetic representations originate in geometry, giving a cohomological criterion for geometric origin.
key_works: Jean-Marc Fontaine and Barry Mazur (1995), *Geometric Galois representations* (identifier verify); Ramla Abdellatif, Supriya Pisolkar, Marine Rougnant and Lara Thomas (2022), *From Fontaine-Mazur conjecture to analytic pro-p groups—a survey*, [arXiv:2205.03558](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03558).

title: Inverse Galois problem over \(\mathbb Q\)
open: Is every finite group the Galois group of some finite Galois extension of the rational numbers? Equivalently, prove that for every finite group \(G\) there exists a finite Galois extension \(L/\mathbb Q\) with \(\operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbb Q) \cong G\), or exhibit a finite group that cannot be so realized.
status: A nineteenth-century question. All finite solvable groups and many nonabelian simple groups are known to be realizable over \(\mathbb Q\); a universal construction remains unknown. Key references: Gunter Malle and B. Heinrich Matzat (1999), *Inverse Galois Theory*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8); Tim Dokchitser, [research resource](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~matyd/InvGal/).
solved_when: Either a proof is given that every finite group occurs as \(\operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbb Q)\) for some finite Galois extension \(L\) of \(\mathbb Q\), or a specific finite group is exhibited together with a proof that it cannot be so realized.
why: A solution would identify the full range of symmetries of polynomial equations over the rationals.
key_works: Gunter Malle and B. Heinrich Matzat (1999), *Inverse Galois Theory*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8); Tim Dokchitser, [research resource](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~matyd/InvGal/).

title: Regular inverse Galois problem
open: Is every finite group \(G\) the Galois group of a regular extension of \(\mathbb Q(t)\) — that is, of a Galois extension \(L/\mathbb Q(t)\) with group \(G\) such that \(L\cap\overline{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\), so the extension acquires no new constant algebraic numbers?
status: Developed in twentieth-century geometric Galois theory: rigidity methods and branched covers realize many groups, but no universal construction working for all finite groups is known. See Gunter Malle and B. Heinrich Matzat (1999), *Inverse Galois Theory*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8).
solved_when: For every finite group \(G\), a Galois extension \(L/\mathbb Q(t)\) is constructed with Galois group \(G\) and \(L\cap\overline{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\).
why: By Hilbert irreducibility, specializing a regular realization yields a Galois extension of \(\mathbb Q\) itself with group \(G\), so a positive answer would resolve the ordinary inverse Galois problem over \(\mathbb Q\).
key_works: Gunter Malle and B. Heinrich Matzat (1999), *Inverse Galois Theory*, [DOI:10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-12123-8).

title: Hilbert’s twelfth problem for arbitrary number fields
open: For arbitrary \(K\), exhibit explicit analytic functions and special arguments whose values generate every finite abelian extension of \(K\), with proved algebraicity and reciprocity laws.
status: Posed in 1900. Cyclotomic and complex-multiplication theories solve classical cases; Dasgupta–Kakde construct maximal abelian extensions of totally real fields using \(p\)-adic integration. Arbitrary fields remain open.
why: Would make class field theory explicit through analytic special values.
key_works: Samit Dasgupta and Mahesh Kakde (2024), *Brumer–Stark Units and Explicit Class Field Theory*, [arXiv:2103.02516](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.02516); ICMS (2024), [*Recent Progress on Hilbert’s 12th Problem*](https://icms.ac.uk/archive/workshop/recent-progress-on-hilberts-12th-problem/).
aliases: Explicit class field theory; generalized Kronecker Jugendtraum.

title: Schinzel’s hypothesis H
open: For finitely many irreducible integer polynomials with positive leading coefficients whose product has no fixed prime divisor, prove that all their values are simultaneously prime infinitely often.
status: Formulated by Schinzel and Sierpiński in 1958 (Andrzej Schinzel and Wacław Sierpiński (1958), *Sur certaines hypothèses concernant les nombres premiers*, [DOI:10.4064/aa-4-3-185-208](https://doi.org/10.4064/aa-4-3-185-208)). Limited linear configurations are accessible; even one quadratic such as \(n^2+1\) is open.
solved_when: A proof that for every such finite family of polynomials, there are infinitely many integers n for which every polynomial in the family takes a prime value at n.
why: It would unify a large family of prime-producing polynomial conjectures, showing the "no fixed prime divisor" condition is the only obstruction.
key_works: Andrzej Schinzel and Wacław Sierpiński (1958), *Sur certaines hypothèses concernant les nombres premiers*, [DOI:10.4064/aa-4-3-185-208](https://doi.org/10.4064/aa-4-3-185-208).

title: Hodge conjecture
open: Which topological cohomology classes on a smooth complex projective variety actually come from algebraic subvarieties? Formally, is every rational cohomology class of type \((p,p)\) a rational linear combination of classes of codimension-\(p\) algebraic subvarieties?
status: The conjecture originates in Hodge's work of the 1930s–1950s. The divisor case and varieties of dimension at most three are covered; higher-codimension cases remain open. Recent work includes Salvatore Floccari and Lie Fu (2025), *The Hodge conjecture for Weil fourfolds with discriminant 1 via singular OG6-varieties*, [arXiv:2504.13607](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13607); the Clay statement is given by Pierre Deligne (2006), *The Hodge Conjecture*, in *The Millennium Prize Problems* ([Clay statement](https://www.claymath.org/millennium/hodge-conjecture/)). A US$1,000,000 Clay Millennium Prize, subject to the institute's rules, is attached.
solved_when: For every smooth complex projective variety and every \(p\), every rational \((p,p)\)-class is proven to be a rational linear combination of codimension-\(p\) algebraic subvariety classes.
why: It would identify precisely which topological cohomology classes arise from algebraic geometry, tying topology to cycles on varieties.
key_works: Pierre Deligne (2006), *The Hodge Conjecture*, in *The Millennium Prize Problems*; [Clay statement](https://www.claymath.org/millennium/hodge-conjecture/); Salvatore Floccari and Lie Fu (2025), *The Hodge conjecture for Weil fourfolds with discriminant 1 via singular OG6-varieties*, [arXiv:2504.13607](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13607).
prize: US$1,000,000 Clay Millennium Prize, subject to the institute’s rules.

solved.paper: The Hodge standard conjecture for self-products of K3 surfaces

title: Generalized Hodge conjecture
open: Can every rational sub-Hodge structure of the cohomology of a smooth projective variety be cut out by an algebraic subset? Formally, given a rational sub-Hodge structure \(V\subset H^k(X,\mathbb Q)\) whose Hodge types have both indices at least \(p\), is there an algebraic subset \(Z\subset X\) of codimension at least \(p\) such that \(V\) restricts to zero on \(X\setminus Z\)?
status: Grothendieck formulated the corrected conjecture in 1969 after identifying a defect in Hodge’s original generalization. Special varieties and degrees are known. Key work: Alexander Grothendieck (1969), *Hodge’s general conjecture is false for trivial reasons*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0040-9383(69)90016-0).
solved_when: For every smooth projective variety \(X\), every \(k\), and every rational sub-Hodge structure \(V\subset H^k(X,\mathbb Q)\) as above, an algebraic subset \(Z\subset X\) of codimension at least \(p\) with \(V\) restricting to zero on \(X\setminus Z\) is exhibited or its existence refuted.
why: It would connect Hodge-theoretic restrictions on cohomology to the actual geometric support of that cohomology by algebraic subsets.
key_works: Alexander Grothendieck (1969), *Hodge’s general conjecture is false for trivial reasons*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0040-9383(69)90016-0).

title: Hodge standard conjecture in positive characteristic
open: Is the signed intersection pairing on the algebraic cycles of a smooth projective variety over a field of positive characteristic positive definite in the expected sense? Formally, does the Hodge standard conjecture (standard conjecture I) hold in positive characteristic?
status: Proposed in the 1960s. Hodge theory handles the characteristic zero case; in positive characteristic, the conjecture is known for surfaces and for abelian fourfolds, the latter by Giuseppe Ancona (2021), *Standard conjectures for abelian fourfolds*, [arXiv:1806.03216](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.03216), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00222-020-00990-7).
solved_when: The positive definiteness of the signed intersection form is proved for all smooth projective varieties over fields of positive characteristic.
why: It would supply the missing positivity principle in the theory of algebraic cycles, completing in positive characteristic what Hodge theory already gives in characteristic zero.
key_works: Giuseppe Ancona (2021), *Standard conjectures for abelian fourfolds*, [arXiv:1806.03216](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.03216), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00222-020-00990-7).
aliases: Standard conjecture I; standard conjecture of Hodge type.

title: Bloch–Beilinson filtration
open: Does every smooth projective variety admit a finite descending filtration on its rational Chow groups, compatible with products and correspondences, whose first step consists of the homologically trivial cycles and whose graded pieces are governed by cohomological motives?
status: The conjecture was developed in the 1980s. Murre's 1993 formulation, using Chow–Künneth projectors, is given in Jacob P. Murre (1993), *On a conjectural filtration on the Chow groups of an algebraic variety. I. The general conjectures and some examples*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0019-3577(93)90038-Z). For curves, surfaces, and special motives, substantial parts of the structure are known.
solved_when: Such a filtration is constructed for arbitrary smooth projective varieties, satisfying compatibility with products and correspondences, with the homologically trivial cycles as the first step and graded pieces governed by cohomological motives.
why: It would organize algebraic cycles by their successive levels of cohomological invisibility, giving the Chow groups the structured layered description that motivic conjectures predict.
key_works: Jacob P. Murre (1993), *On a conjectural filtration on the Chow groups of an algebraic variety. I. The general conjectures and some examples*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/0019-3577(93)90038-Z).

title: Bloch’s zero-cycle conjecture for surfaces with \(p_g=0\)
open: Is every smooth projective complex surface of geometric genus zero determined, in its zero-cycle theory, by its Albanese variety? Formally, prove that the Albanese map \(CH_0(S)^0\to\operatorname{Alb}(S)(\mathbb C)\) is an isomorphism for every such surface \(S\).
status: The conjecture was formulated in the 1970s. It is known outside general type and for numerous special general-type families. Key works include Kalyan Banerjee (2025), *Bloch’s conjecture on certain surfaces of general type with \(p_g=0\) and with an involution: The Enriques case*, [publication](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0019357725000321); and Vladimir Guletskii and Claudio Pedrini (2003), *Finite dimensional motives and the Conjectures of Beilinson and Murre*, [arXiv:math/0303170](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0303170).
solved_when: The Albanese map \(CH_0(S)^0\to\operatorname{Alb}(S)(\mathbb C)\) is proven to be an isomorphism for every smooth projective complex surface \(S\) with \(p_g=0\).
why: It would show that zero-cycles on these surfaces carry no hidden information beyond the Albanese variety, reducing their cycle theory to an abelian variety.
key_works: Kalyan Banerjee (2025), *Bloch’s conjecture on certain surfaces of general type with \(p_g=0\) and with an involution: The Enriques case*, [publication](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0019357725000321); Vladimir Guletskii and Claudio Pedrini (2003), *Finite dimensional motives and the Conjectures of Beilinson and Murre*, [arXiv:math/0303170](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0303170).

title: Kimura–O’Sullivan finite-dimensionality
open: Is every smooth projective variety's rational Chow motive finite-dimensional in Kimura and O'Sullivan's sense — that is, expressible as a direct sum \(M_+\oplus M_-\) where some exterior power of \(M_+\) and some symmetric power of \(M_-\) vanishes?
status: Proposed around 2000. The property is known for motives of curves, abelian varieties, and varieties generated from them by appropriate motivic operations. Key works: Shun-ichi Kimura (2005), *Chow groups are finite dimensional, in some sense*, [DOI:10.1007/s00208-004-0577-3](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00208-004-0577-3); Guletskii and Pedrini (2003), [arXiv:math/0303170](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0303170).
solved_when: A proof (or construction) is given showing that every smooth projective variety admits a Chow-motive decomposition \(M_+\oplus M_-\) with some exterior power of \(M_+\) and some symmetric power of \(M_-\) equal to zero.
why: Finite-dimensionality would impose strong finiteness and nilpotence properties on algebraic correspondences, giving control over the motivic behavior of cycles.
key_works: Shun-ichi Kimura (2005), *Chow groups are finite dimensional, in some sense*, [DOI:10.1007/s00208-004-0577-3](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00208-004-0577-3); Guletskii and Pedrini (2003), [arXiv:math/0303170](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0303170).

title: Resolution of singularities in positive characteristic
open: Does every integral variety over a perfect field of positive characteristic admit resolution of singularities? Formally, must there exist a proper birational morphism from a smooth variety that is an isomorphism over the original smooth locus?
status: Characteristic-zero resolution was proved in 1964. Low dimensions are known; the general problem from dimension four upward remains open. Alterations are generically finite and do not supply the required birational map. See Herwig Hauser (2010), *On the problem of resolution of singularities in positive characteristic (Or: A proof we are still waiting for)*, [DOI:10.1090/S0273-0979-09-01274-9](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0273-0979-09-01274-9).
solved_when: Such a proper birational morphism is constructed for every integral variety over a perfect field of positive characteristic, in all dimensions from four upward where the problem remains open.
why: It would extend many geometric constructions and arguments to positive characteristic, where they currently fail for lack of birational resolution.
key_works: Herwig Hauser (2010), *On the problem of resolution of singularities in positive characteristic (Or: A proof we are still waiting for)*, [DOI:10.1090/S0273-0979-09-01274-9](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0273-0979-09-01274-9).

title: Strong factorization of birational maps
open: Given a birational map between smooth complete characteristic-zero varieties, find a smooth common model obtained from each solely by blowups along smooth centers.
status: Classical. Weak factorization, allowing interspersed blowups and blowdowns, was established around 2000; ordering all blowups before all blowdowns remains open.
why: Would provide a more rigid and constructive description of birational equivalence.
key_works: Dan Abramovich, Kalle Karu, Kenji Matsuki and Jarosław Włodarczyk (2002), *Torification and Factorization of Birational Maps*, [arXiv:math/9904135](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9904135), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-02-00396-X).

title: Abundance conjecture
open: If a projective Kawamata log terminal pair \((X,\Delta)\) in characteristic zero has rational boundary and nef \(K_X+\Delta\), must some positive integral multiple of \(K_X+\Delta\) be base-point-free? Equivalently, does numerical semiampleness of the log canonical divisor follow from these hypotheses?
status: The conjecture has been central to the minimal model program since the 1980s; it is established through dimension three and in many higher-dimensional special cases. See János Kollár and Shigefumi Mori (1998), *Birational Geometry of Algebraic Varieties*, [DOI:10.1017/CBO9780511662560](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511662560).
solved_when: For every projective klt pair \((X,\Delta)\) in characteristic zero with rational boundary and nef \(K_X+\Delta\), there exists a positive integer \(m\) such that \(m(K_X+\Delta)\) is base-point-free.
why: It would convert numerical positivity of the canonical divisor into an actual geometric fibration, giving the output of the minimal model program a concrete structure.
key_works: János Kollár and Shigefumi Mori (1998), *Birational Geometry of Algebraic Varieties*, [DOI:10.1017/CBO9780511662560](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511662560).

title: Nagata’s plane-curve conjecture
open: For a nonsquare number \(r\ge10\) of very general points in \(\mathbb P^2_{\mathbb C}\), must every curve of degree \(d\) passing through them with multiplicities \(m_i\) satisfy \(d\ge(\sum_i m_i)/\sqrt r\)? In other words, is Nagata's proposed lower bound on the degree of plane curves with prescribed high multiplicities at very general points true in every nonsquare case?
status: The conjecture was proposed in 1959. Nagata proved the corresponding case where \(r\) is a square; the nonsquare cases begin with ten points. Recent work includes Carlos Galindo, Francisco Monserrat, Carlos-Jesús Moreno-Ávila and Julio José Moyano-Fernández (2025), *On the valuative Nagata conjecture*, [arXiv:2208.11041](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.11041), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40687-025-00500-2).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of the inequality \(d\ge(\sum_i m_i)/\sqrt r\) for every nonsquare \(r\ge10\) and every very general configuration of \(r\) points in \(\mathbb P^2_{\mathbb C}\), together with any multiplicity specification \(m_i\).
why: It would determine the fundamental limits on interpolation by plane algebraic curves: how much multiplicity at very general points a curve of fixed degree can carry.
key_works: Carlos Galindo, Francisco Monserrat, Carlos-Jesús Moreno-Ávila and Julio José Moyano-Fernández (2025), *On the valuative Nagata conjecture*, [arXiv:2208.11041](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.11041), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40687-025-00500-2).

title: Segre–Harbourne–Gimigliano–Hirschowitz conjecture
open: Is every special linear system of plane curves with assigned multiplicities at very general points accounted for by fixed \((-1)\)-curves — that is, after removing the forced \((-1)\)-components, does the system have exactly its expected dimension?
status: The conjecture originates with Segre in 1961, with later refinements. Many bounded-multiplicity and homogeneous cases are settled, but arbitrary multiplicity lists remain open. Key work: Maria Chiara Brambilla and Elisa Postinghel (2025), *Towards Good Postulation of Fat Points, One Step at a Time*, [DOI:10.1007/s40574-025-00468-5](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40574-025-00468-5).
solved_when: For every multiplicity list, the dimension of the linear system equals the expected dimension after subtracting the contributions of the fixed \((-1)\)-curves.
why: It would classify all failures of expected dimension in plane-curve interpolation, reducing postulation behavior to an explicit geometric mechanism.
key_works: Maria Chiara Brambilla and Elisa Postinghel (2025), *Towards Good Postulation of Fat Points, One Step at a Time*, [DOI:10.1007/s40574-025-00468-5](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40574-025-00468-5).

title: Hartshorne complete-intersection conjecture
open: Must every smooth complex projective variety in projective space whose dimension far exceeds its codimension be cut out by exactly as many equations as its codimension? Formally: is every smooth complex projective \(X\subset\mathbb P^{n+c}\) of dimension \(n\ge2c+1\) a complete intersection?
status: Proposed in 1974. Important classes, including varieties defined by quadrics, are known; the general small-codimension case remains open. Key works: Robin Hartshorne (1974), *Varieties of small codimension in projective space*; Kiwamu Watanabe (2025), *Quadratic Varieties of Small Codimension*, [arXiv:2405.04002](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04002), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.3842/SIGMA.2025.045).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the statement that every smooth complex projective \(X\subset\mathbb P^{n+c}\) with \(n\ge2c+1\) is a complete intersection.
why: It would show that sufficiently low codimension forces an exceptionally simple equation structure — the variety is defined by the minimal possible number of equations.
key_works: Robin Hartshorne (1974), *Varieties of small codimension in projective space* (identifier verify); Kiwamu Watanabe (2025), *Quadratic Varieties of Small Codimension*, [arXiv:2405.04002](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04002), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.3842/SIGMA.2025.045).

title: Existence of Ulrich bundles
open: Does every smooth projective variety, equipped with a fixed very ample polarization \(\mathcal O_X(1)\), carry a nonzero Ulrich vector bundle — one satisfying \(H^i(X,E(-j))=0\) for all \(0\le i\le\dim X\) and \(1\le j\le\dim X\)?
status: The problem has been prominent since the early 2000s, and Ulrich bundles are known to exist for many curves, surfaces, homogeneous varieties, and double-cover cases; N. Mohan Kumar, Poornapushkala Narayanan and A. J. Parameswaran (2025), *Ulrich bundles on double covers of projective spaces*, [arXiv:2201.08703](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.08703), contributes to the double-cover cases.
solved_when: An explicit construction (or existence proof) of such a nonzero vector bundle \(E\) is given for an arbitrary smooth projective variety with its fixed very ample \(\mathcal O_X(1)\), satisfying the vanishing \(H^i(X,E(-j))=0\) for all \(0\le i\le\dim X\) and \(1\le j\le\dim X\).
why: A solution would supply optimally behaved vector bundles and linear algebraic presentations on every polarized variety, making the geometry of arbitrary polarizations accessible to commutative-algebraic and homological methods.
key_works: N. Mohan Kumar, Poornapushkala Narayanan and A. J. Parameswaran (2025), *Ulrich bundles on double covers of projective spaces*, [arXiv:2201.08703](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.08703).

title: Cancellation for affine three-space in characteristic zero
open: If an affine complex variety \(X\) satisfies \(X\times\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^4\), must \(X\cong\mathbb A^3\)? That is, does Zariski cancellation hold for affine three-space over \(\mathbb C\)?
status: Zariski’s question dates to the mid-twentieth century. Cancellation is known in dimensions one and two. Gupta’s positive-characteristic counterexamples — Neena Gupta (2014), *On Zariski’s Cancellation Problem in positive characteristic*, [arXiv:1309.1368](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.1368) — leave the characteristic-zero three-dimensional case open; see also Parnashree Ghosh (2026), [IISc seminar on cancellation](https://math.iisc.ac.in/seminars/2026/2026-04-22-parnashree-ghosh.html).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that \(X\times\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^4\) with \(X\) a complex affine variety forces \(X\cong\mathbb A^3\).
why: It would determine whether an affine-line factor can conceal nontrivial algebraic geometry in dimension three over \(\mathbb C\).
key_works: Neena Gupta (2014), *On Zariski’s Cancellation Problem in positive characteristic*, [arXiv:1309.1368](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.1368); Parnashree Ghosh (2026), [IISc seminar on cancellation](https://math.iisc.ac.in/seminars/2026/2026-04-22-parnashree-ghosh.html).

title: Huneke–Wiegand torsion conjecture
open: If \(R\) is a one-dimensional Gorenstein local domain and \(M\) is a nonfree finitely generated torsion-free \(R\)-module, must \(M\otimes_R\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\) always contain torsion?
status: Conjectured in 1994. Hypersurface cases and numerous special modules are understood, but the conjecture remains open in general for higher-codimension complete intersections. Key works: Craig Huneke and Roger Wiegand (1994), *Tensor products of modules and the rigidity of Tor*; Rafael Holanda and Cleto B. Miranda-Neto (2025), *An Ext-Tor duality theorem, cohomological dimension, and applications*, arXiv:2312.09725.
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, is given for the general statement over every one-dimensional Gorenstein local domain; in particular, the higher-codimension complete intersection case is settled.
why: A solution would tie the torsion behavior of tensor products directly to questions of freeness and rigidity of modules over such rings.
key_works: Craig Huneke and Roger Wiegand (1994), *Tensor products of modules and the rigidity of Tor*, [record](https://geodesic.mathdoc.fr/item/MAN_1994__299_4_165218/); Rafael Holanda and Cleto B. Miranda-Neto (2025), *An Ext-Tor duality theorem, cohomological dimension, and applications*, [arXiv:2312.09725](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.09725).

title: Eisenbud–Mazur symbolic-square conjecture
open: If a prime \(P\) lives in a regular local ring \((R,\mathfrak m)\) containing \(\mathbb Q\), must its symbolic square \(P^{(2)}=P^2R_P\cap R\) always lie inside \(\mathfrak m P\)? In other words, is every element of the second symbolic power of \(P\) an infinitesimal deformation of an element of \(P\) itself?
status: Proposed in the 1990s by David Eisenbud and Barry Mazur (1997), *Evolutions, Symbolic Squares, and Fitting Ideals*, [arXiv:alg-geom/9511008](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9511008), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1997.488.189). Low-codimension and linkage cases are known; positive-characteristic analogues of the statement can fail.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of \(P^{(2)}\subseteq\mathfrak mP\) for all primes \(P\) in every regular local ring containing \(\mathbb Q\).
why: A proof would constrain infinitesimal deformations of ideals and clarify how far symbolic and ordinary powers of a prime can diverge, a basic gap in commutative algebra.
key_works: David Eisenbud and Barry Mazur (1997), *Evolutions, Symbolic Squares, and Fitting Ideals*, [arXiv:alg-geom/9511008](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9511008), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1997.488.189).

title: Lech’s multiplicity conjecture in mixed characteristic
open: Can a flat local extension of a Noetherian local ring ever lower the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity when the base ring has mixed characteristic? Formally: for every flat local map \(R\to S\) of Noetherian local rings with \(R\) of mixed characteristic, prove \(e(R)\le e(S)\).
status: Proposed in 1960. Low-dimensional and special cases are known. Linquan Ma (2017), *Lech's conjecture in dimension three*, [arXiv:1609.00095](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.00095); Srikanth B. Iyengar, Linquan Ma and Mark Walker (2026), *Lech's conjecture in equal characteristic*, [preliminary exposition](https://mark-walker-22.github.io/Lech.html) — an October 6, 2026 preliminary exposition addresses equal characteristic, while mixed characteristic remains a separate target.
solved_when: The inequality \(e(R)\le e(S)\) holds for all flat local maps \(R\to S\) of Noetherian local rings in which \(R\) has mixed characteristic.
why: It would establish that flat extension cannot reduce this measure of local singularity complexity.
key_works: Linquan Ma (2017), *Lech’s conjecture in dimension three*, [arXiv:1609.00095](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.00095); Srikanth B. Iyengar, Linquan Ma and Mark Walker (2026), *Lech’s conjecture in equal characteristic*, [preliminary exposition](https://mark-walker-22.github.io/Lech.html).

title: Ramanujan conjecture for Hecke–Maass forms
open: Is the Ramanujan conjecture true for Hecke–Maass cusp forms — that is, does every normalized Hecke–Maass cusp form on \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathbb H\) satisfy \(|\lambda_f(p)|\le 2\) for every prime \(p\), in unitary normalization?
status: The Maass-form extension of Ramanujan’s problem remains open. The best result is Kim–Sarnak’s exponent \(7/64\), giving \(|\lambda_f(p)|\le p^{7/64}+p^{-7/64}\) (Henry H. Kim and Peter Sarnak, 2003, *Refined estimates towards the Ramanujan and Selberg conjectures*, Appendix 2 to Kim’s functoriality paper, [DOI:10.1090/S0894-0347-02-00410-1](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-02-00410-1)).
solved_when: The bound \(|\lambda_f(p)|\le 2\) is proved for every prime \(p\) and every normalized Hecke–Maass cusp form on \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathbb H\) in unitary normalization.
why: It would give optimal local bounds for these automorphic representations.
key_works: Henry H. Kim and Peter Sarnak (2003), *Refined estimates towards the Ramanujan and Selberg conjectures*, Appendix 2 to Kim’s functoriality paper, [DOI:10.1090/S0894-0347-02-00410-1](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-02-00410-1).

title: Mumford–Tate conjecture for abelian varieties
open: For every abelian variety over a number field, prove that the identity component of its \(\ell\)-adic algebraic monodromy group equals its Mumford–Tate group over \(\mathbb Q_\ell\).
status: The conjecture was proposed in the 1960s. It is known for elliptic curves, CM abelian varieties, and many additional classes; the case of arbitrary dimension remains open. Background and partial results are surveyed in Victoria Cantoral Farfán (2016), *A survey around the Hodge, Tate and Mumford-Tate conjectures for abelian varieties*, [arXiv:1602.08354](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.08354); see also Richard Pink (1998), *l-adic algebraic monodromy groups, cocharacters, and the Mumford-Tate conjecture*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1998.018).
solved_when: The equality between the identity component of the \(\ell\)-adic algebraic monodromy group and the Mumford–Tate group (base-changed to \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)) is proved for every abelian variety over a number field, with no restriction on dimension.
why: A solution would identify the compatibility between Hodge-theoretic and Galois-theoretic symmetries, showing that the symmetries visible in the Hodge structure govern exactly the Galois symmetries of the \(\ell\)-adic cohomology.
key_works: Victoria Cantoral Farfán (2016), *A survey around the Hodge, Tate and Mumford-Tate conjectures for abelian varieties*, [arXiv:1602.08354](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.08354); Richard Pink (1998), *l-adic algebraic monodromy groups, cocharacters, and the Mumford-Tate conjecture*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1998.018).

title: Broué’s abelian-defect-group conjecture
open: Is every block of a finite group algebra with abelian defect group derived-equivalent to its Brauer correspondent? Formally, for a block with abelian defect group \(D\), prove its bounded derived module category is equivalent to that of the corresponding block of the normalizer \(N_G(D)\).
status: Proposed in 1990 by Michel Broué (*Isométries parfaites, types de blocs, catégories dérivées*, [original](https://numdam.org/item/AST_1990__181-182__61_0/); see also Jeremy Rickard's [problem statement](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~majcr/adgc/what.html)). Cyclic-defect blocks and many group families are known; arbitrary abelian-defect blocks remain open.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) covering arbitrary blocks with abelian defect groups, establishing the derived equivalence with the Brauer-correspondent block in \(N_G(D)\) in full generality.
why: It would relate global modular representation theory to local subgroup data, reducing questions about blocks to their local structure.
key_works: Michel Broué (1990), *Isométries parfaites, types de blocs, catégories dérivées*, [original](https://numdam.org/item/AST_1990__181-182__61_0/); Jeremy Rickard, [problem statement](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~majcr/adgc/what.html).

title: Goldberg conjecture in negative scalar curvature
open: Must every compact Einstein almost-Kähler manifold be Kähler? The remaining unresolved case is negative scalar curvature, where the compatible almost-complex structure is nonintegrable.
status: Conjectured in 1969. Sekigawa proved the nonnegative-scalar-curvature case in 1987 [Kouei Sekigawa (1987), *On some compact Einstein almost Kähler manifolds*]; noncompact examples do not settle the compact case. See also Vestislav Apostolov and Tedi Drăghici (2003), *The curvature and the integrability of almost-Kähler manifolds: a survey*, [arXiv:math/0302152](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0302152).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) covering the negative-scalar-curvature case with a nonintegrable compatible almost-complex structure is given.
why: It would establish a strong compatibility between Einstein geometry and symplectic structure.
key_works: Kouei Sekigawa (1987), *On some compact Einstein almost Kähler manifolds*; Vestislav Apostolov and Tedi Drăghici (2003), *The curvature and the integrability of almost-Kähler manifolds: a survey*, [arXiv:math/0302152](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0302152).

title: Chern’s discreteness conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces
open: For a fixed dimension \(n\), can a closed minimal hypersurface of the sphere \(S^{n+1}\) realize only a discrete set of constant scalar curvature values? Formally: is the set of constant scalar curvatures attained by closed minimal hypersurfaces of \(S^{n+1}\) discrete?
status: The problem originates in Chern’s questions from the 1960s–1980s. Simons-type gap theorems, following James Simons (1968), *Minimal varieties in Riemannian manifolds*, exclude intervals of possible curvature values but do not establish global discreteness. Recent related work includes Jianquan Ge and Fagui Li (2021; revised 2025), *Integral-Einstein hypersurfaces in spheres*, [arXiv:2101.03753](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.03753).
solved_when: For each fixed \(n\), the set of constant scalar curvatures realized by closed minimal hypersurfaces of \(S^{n+1}\) is shown to be discrete (or a counterexample hypersurface family is produced).
why: A positive answer would impose a discrete structure on the constant-curvature minimal hypersurfaces of spheres, constraining which geometric spectra are geometrically realizable.
key_works: James Simons (1968), *Minimal varieties in Riemannian manifolds*; Jianquan Ge and Fagui Li (2021; revised 2025), *Integral-Einstein hypersurfaces in spheres*, [arXiv:2101.03753](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.03753).
aliases: Chern conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces in spheres.

title: Infinitely many prime closed geodesics on higher-dimensional spheres
open: Does every smooth Riemannian metric on \(S^n\), \(n\ge3\), possess infinitely many geometrically distinct prime closed geodesics?
status: This is a classical twentieth-century problem. The two-sphere case is settled, and loop-space topology yields powerful sufficient conditions for infinitely many prime closed geodesics — but these conditions do not cover arbitrary metrics on higher-dimensional spheres.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that every smooth Riemannian metric on \(S^n\), \(n\ge3\), either has infinitely many geometrically distinct prime closed geodesics or fails to, for all such metrics.
why: A positive answer would establish unavoidable complexity in geodesic dynamics on spheres: no metric on a higher-dimensional sphere can tame its geodesic flow to finitely many prime closed orbits.
key_works: Detlef Gromoll and Wolfgang Meyer (1969), *Periodic geodesics on compact Riemannian manifolds*; Keith Burns and Vladimir Matveev (2013; updated 2019), *Open problems and questions about geodesics*, [arXiv:1308.5417](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.5417).

title: Smooth Hamiltonian Seifert problem in four dimensions
open: Does there exist a \(C^\infty\) Hamiltonian on \(\mathbb R^4\) admitting a compact regular energy hypersurface on which no trajectory is periodic? Equivalently, can the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture fail in four dimensions even under full smoothness?
status: Smooth examples exist in higher dimensions. Viktor Ginzburg and Başak Gürel (2003), *A C2-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in R4*, [arXiv:math/0110047](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0110047), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2003.158.953), constructed a \(C^2\) example in dimension four; the \(C^\infty\) case remains open.
solved_when: A \(C^\infty\) Hamiltonian on \(\mathbb R^4\) is exhibited together with a compact regular energy hypersurface containing no periodic orbit; or a proof is given that no such Hamiltonian exists, so every compact regular energy hypersurface of a smooth Hamiltonian on \(\mathbb R^4\) carries a periodic trajectory.
why: It settles whether smoothness alone forces periodic dynamics at the four-dimensional boundary, the critical case between the known higher-dimensional counterexamples and the smooth category.
key_works: Viktor Ginzburg and Başak Gürel (2003), *A C2-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in R4*, [arXiv:math/0110047](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0110047), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2003.158.953).

title: Smooth four-dimensional Schoenflies conjecture
open: Does every smoothly embedded three-sphere in the four-sphere bound a standard smooth four-ball on each side? Equivalently, is each complementary region of a smooth embedding \(S^3\hookrightarrow S^4\) diffeomorphic to the standard four-ball?
status: The remaining smooth dimension is longstanding. Topological Schoenflies is known; recent work connects the smooth problem to pseudo-isotopies of \(S^1\times S^3\). Key works: Morton Brown (1960), *A proof of the generalized Schoenflies theorem*; David Gabai (2022), *3-Spheres in the 4-Sphere and Pseudo-Isotopies of S1×S3*, [arXiv:2212.02004](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.02004).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that both complementary components of any smooth embedding \(S^3\hookrightarrow S^4\) are diffeomorphic to the standard smooth four-ball.
why: It would classify the smooth regions cut out by embedded three-spheres in \(S^4\), settling the last smooth case of the Schoenflies problem.
key_works: Morton Brown (1960), *A proof of the generalized Schoenflies theorem*; David Gabai (2022), *3-Spheres in the 4-Sphere and Pseudo-Isotopies of S1×S3*, [arXiv:2212.02004](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.02004).
aliases: Smooth Schoenflies problem in dimension four.

title: Eleven-eighths conjecture
open: Does every closed smooth spin four-manifold satisfy \(b_2(X) \ge (11/8)|\sigma(X)|\)? Equivalently, is the second Betti number of such a manifold always at least eleven-eighths of the absolute value of its signature?
status: The conjecture is attributed to Matsumoto in 1982. Furuta (Mikio Furuta (2001), *Monopole equation and the 11/8-conjecture*) proved the ten-eighths inequality with an additive correction, and later equivariant refinements — e.g. Michael Hopkins, Jianfeng Lin, XiaoLin Danny Shi and Zhouli Xu (2022), *Intersection Forms of Spin 4-Manifolds and the Pin(2)-Equivariant Mahowald Invariant*, [arXiv:1812.04052](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.04052) — improve particular congruence classes.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the inequality \(b_2(X)\ge(11/8)|\sigma(X)|\) holding for every closed smooth spin four-manifold \(X\).
why: The inequality would sharply constrain which intersection forms can arise from smooth spin four-manifolds, cutting the space of possible forms well beyond known bounds.
key_works: Mikio Furuta (2001), *Monopole equation and the 11/8-conjecture*; Michael Hopkins, Jianfeng Lin, XiaoLin Danny Shi and Zhouli Xu (2022), *Intersection Forms of Spin 4-Manifolds and the Pin(2)-Equivariant Mahowald Invariant*, [arXiv:1812.04052](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.04052).

title: Exotic smooth structure on the complex projective plane
open: Does there exist a smooth four-manifold that is homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to the complex projective plane \(\mathbb{CP}^2\)? In other words, can the simplest simply connected closed four-manifold carry an exotic smooth structure?
status: Open since the emergence of exotic simply connected four-manifolds in the 1980s. Exotic smooth structures are known to exist on many blowups of \(\mathbb{CP}^2\), but the unblown-up projective plane itself remains unresolved. Key works: Robion Kirby (1997), *Problems in low-dimensional topology*, [author collection](https://math.berkeley.edu/~kirby/); Robert Gompf and András Stipsicz (1999), *4-Manifolds and Kirby Calculus*.
solved_when: A smooth four-manifold is exhibited that is homeomorphic to \(\mathbb{CP}^2\) but not diffeomorphic to it; alternatively, a proof that no such manifold exists resolves the problem.
why: A positive answer would locate the smallest possible complexity of exotic simply connected smooth four-manifolds, sharpening the boundary of where exotic phenomena begin in dimension four.
key_works: Robion Kirby (1997), *Problems in low-dimensional topology*, [author collection](https://math.berkeley.edu/~kirby/); Robert Gompf and András Stipsicz (1999), *4-Manifolds and Kirby Calculus*.

title: Geometric simple connectivity of closed simply connected four-manifolds
open: Does every closed simply connected smooth four-manifold have a handle decomposition involving no 1-handles, without needing to stabilize the manifold first? Equivalently, must geometric simple connectivity — visible directly in the handle structure — hold for all closed simply connected four-manifolds?
status: This is a classical problem from Kirby's problem list. Many examples of closed simply connected four-manifolds are known to admit such decompositions, and while boundary counterexamples exist, they do not resolve the closed case. Key works: Robion Kirby (1997), *Problems in low-dimensional topology*; Kouichi Yasui (2019), *Geometrically simply connected 4-manifolds and stable cohomotopy Seiberg-Witten invariants*, [arXiv:1807.11453](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.11453).
solved_when: A proof that every closed simply connected smooth four-manifold admits a handle decomposition without one-handles and without stabilization, or an explicit counterexample of such a manifold requiring stabilization to eliminate its one-handles.
