why: A positive answer would make algebraic simple connectivity visible directly in the handle structure, turning a homotopy-theoretic condition into a hands-on geometric one for four-manifold handle calculus.
key_works: Robion Kirby (1997), *Problems in low-dimensional topology*; Kouichi Yasui (2019), *Geometrically simply connected 4-manifolds and stable cohomotopy Seiberg-Witten invariants*, [arXiv:1807.11453](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.11453).

title: Topological surgery in dimension four for arbitrary fundamental groups
open: When a degree-one normal map of four-manifolds has vanishing Wall surgery obstruction, must it be normally bordant to a homotopy equivalence, without restricting the fundamental group to known good classes?
status: Freedman's theory and later work handle large classes of fundamental groups, including those of subexponential growth; free fundamental groups remain central test cases. Key works include Michael Freedman and Frank Quinn (1990), *Topology of 4-Manifolds*, and Freedman and Vyacheslav Krushkal (2016), *Engel relations in 4-manifold topology*, [arXiv:1412.5024](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5024).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for arbitrary fundamental groups: every degree-one normal map of four-manifolds with vanishing surgery obstruction is normally bordant to a homotopy equivalence, with no restriction on the group.
why: A positive answer would extend the principal classification method for high-dimensional manifolds to unrestricted four-dimensional topology.
key_works: Michael Freedman and Frank Quinn (1990), *Topology of 4-Manifolds*; Freedman and Vyacheslav Krushkal (2016), *Engel relations in 4-manifold topology*, [arXiv:1412.5024](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5024).

title: Jones polynomial detection of the unknot
open: If the normalized Jones polynomial of a knot is \(1\), must the knot be the unknot? In other words, does the Jones polynomial detect the simplest knot type?
status: Open since the invariant's introduction in 1984–1985. Many families and finite tables have been checked. Khovanov homology detects the unknot — Peter Kronheimer and Tomasz Mrowka (2011), *Khovanov homology is an unknot-detector*, [arXiv:1005.4346](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.4346) — but that stronger invariant does not settle this question. The polynomial itself originates with Vaughan Jones (1985), *A polynomial invariant for knots via von Neumann algebras*.
solved_when: A proof that any knot whose normalized Jones polynomial equals \(1\) is the unknot, or an explicit counterexample knot with Jones polynomial \(1\) that is knotted.
why: It would determine whether the Jones polynomial — the invariant from which much of modern quantum topology grew — detects the simplest knot type, a basic structural question the invariant has resisted since its introduction.
key_works: Vaughan Jones (1985), *A polynomial invariant for knots via von Neumann algebras*; Peter Kronheimer and Tomasz Mrowka (2011), *Khovanov homology is an unknot-detector*, [arXiv:1005.4346](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.4346).

title: Volume conjecture for hyperbolic knots
open: Does the hyperbolic volume of every hyperbolic knot emerge from the asymptotics of its colored Jones polynomial? Formally, is Kashaev's limit — the limit of the colored Jones polynomial evaluated at roots of unity — equal to the hyperbolic volume of the knot complement for every hyperbolic knot \(K\)?
status: Kashaev proposed the volume-growth phenomenon in 1997 (Rinat Kashaev (1997), *The hyperbolic volume of knots from quantum dilogarithm*, [arXiv:q-alg/9601025](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9601025)), and Murakami–Murakami connected it to colored Jones polynomials in 2001 (Hitoshi Murakami and Jun Murakami (2001), *The colored Jones polynomials and the simplicial volume of a knot*, [arXiv:math/9905075](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9905075)). The conjecture is currently verified only for selected knots and families.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given for every hyperbolic knot, not merely selected knots and families; the natural criterion is a complete verification or counterexample to the volume conjecture as stated for the class of all hyperbolic knots.
why: A proof would recover hyperbolic geometry — the classical metric structure of the knot complement — purely from the asymptotics of quantum invariants, establishing a rigorous bridge between quantum topology and hyperbolic geometry.
key_works: Rinat Kashaev (1997), *The hyperbolic volume of knots from quantum dilogarithm*, [arXiv:q-alg/9601025](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-alg/9601025); Hitoshi Murakami and Jun Murakami (2001), *The colored Jones polynomials and the simplicial volume of a knot*, [arXiv:math/9905075](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9905075).

title: Bernhard Riemann
open: Does the prime-counting function ever exceed the logarithmic integral — that is, what is the smallest x with π(x) > li(x)? Riemann, at the end of his 1859 paper "[[On the Number of Primes Less Than a Given Magnitude]]", stated (based on his results) that li(x) somewhat overestimates π(x), and the evidence seemed to agree; yet J. E. Littlewood proved in 1914 that this fails infinitely often, so the question is where the first crossover actually lies.
status: Riemann's 1859 claim was disproved in 1914 by J. E. Littlewood, and it is now known that the first x with π(x) > li(x) occurs somewhere before 10317; see [[Skewes' number]] for more detail. The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: An explicit value of the first x for which π(x) > li(x) is determined; currently only the bound "somewhere before 10317" is known (see [[Skewes' number]]).

title: Casas-Alvero conjecture
open: If a polynomial of degree d over a field K of characteristic 0 shares a common factor with each of its derivatives up to order d − 1, must it be the d-th power of a linear polynomial?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics as of 2026-10-07 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that every degree-d polynomial over a characteristic-0 field sharing a common factor with all of its first d − 1 derivatives is necessarily the d-th power of a linear polynomial.

title: Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture
open: If a group has cohomological dimension 2, must it admit a 2-dimensional Eilenberg–MacLane space K(G, 1)?
solved_when: A proof that every group of cohomological dimension 2 admits a K(G, 1) complex of dimension 2, or a counterexample of such a group with no 2-dimensional K(G, 1).

title: Farrell–Jones conjecture
open: Is the Farrell–Jones conjecture true — that is, are the relevant assembly maps isomorphisms as the conjecture asserts?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the conjecture that the assembly maps in question are isomorphisms.

title: Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture
open: Does a local–global (Hasse-type) principle hold for linear ordinary differential equations, in the sense that a system with vanishing p-curvature for almost all primes p must admit a full set of algebraic solutions?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture is given: vanishing p-curvature for almost all primes implies the existence of a basis of algebraic solutions.

title: Hadamard conjecture
open: Does a Hadamard matrix of order 4k exist for every positive integer k?
solved_when: A construction (or existence proof) of a Hadamard matrix of order 4k is given for every positive integer k, or a counterexample k is exhibited.

title: Hadamard's maximal determinant problem
open: What is the largest possible determinant of an $n \times n$ matrix whose entries are all $1$ or $-1$? Equally, determine (or sharply bound) $\max\{|\det A| : A \in \{\pm 1\}^{n \times n}\}$ for each order $n$.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: A complete characterization of the maximal determinant as a function of the matrix order $n$ is available; short of that, any resolution of the cases where the maximum is currently unknown counts as substantial progress.

title: Jacobson's conjecture
open: Must the powers of the Jacobson radical of a ring that is Noetherian on both sides eventually intersect in zero? Formally, Jacobson's conjecture asserts that ⋂ₙ J(R)ⁿ = 0 for every left-and-right Noetherian ring R.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, showing that the intersection of all powers of the Jacobson radical of a left-and-right Noetherian ring is, or need not be, zero.

title: Pierce–Birkhoff conjecture
open: Is every piecewise-polynomial function from \mathbb{R}^{n} to \mathbb{R} representable as the maximum of a finite set of minimums of finite collections of polynomials? Formally, the conjecture asks whether every such f can be written in the form \max_{i} \min_{j} p_{ij} with the p_{ij} polynomials.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every piecewise-polynomial f:\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R} equals the maximum of a finite set of minimums of finite collections of polynomials, for arbitrary n.

title: Rota's basis conjecture
open: Given a matroid of rank n with n disjoint bases, can the elements always be arranged into an n × n array whose rows are the given bases and whose columns are themselves bases of the matroid?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that for every matroid of rank n with n disjoint bases, the elements can be permuted so that each of the n columns forms a basis.

title: Serre's conjecture II
open: Does Galois cohomology in degree one vanish for every simply connected semisimple algebraic group over a "small" field? Formally: if G is a simply connected semisimple algebraic group over a perfect field F of cohomological dimension at most 2, is the Galois cohomology set H^{1}(F, G) necessarily trivial?
status: The problem, known as Serre's conjecture II, is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (as of 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that H^{1}(F, G) = 0 for every simply connected semisimple algebraic group G over every perfect field F of cohomological dimension at most 2.

title: Serre's positivity conjecture
open: If R is a commutative regular local ring and P, Q are prime ideals of R with dim(R/P) + dim(R/Q) = dim(R), must the intersection multiplicity χ(R/P, R/Q) be strictly positive?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that dim(R/P) + dim(R/Q) = dim(R) implies χ(R/P, R/Q) > 0 for every regular local ring R and prime ideals P, Q.

title: Zariski–Lipman conjecture
open: If the module of derivations of the coordinate ring of a complex algebraic variety is free over that ring, must the variety be smooth? In formal terms, the conjecture predicts that freeness of Der(R) as an R-module forces R to be a regular ring.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of the statement: for every complex algebraic variety V with coordinate ring R such that Der(R) is a free R-module, V is smooth.

title: Andrews–Curtis conjecture
open: Can every balanced presentation of the trivial group be reduced to the trivial presentation using only Nielsen transformations on the relators and conjugations of relators?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof via an explicit balanced presentation of the trivial group not reducible by such moves) is established.

title: Bounded Burnside problem
open: for which positive integers m, n is the free Burnside group  finite? In particular, is  finite?

title: Herzog–Schönheim conjecture
open: Can a finite group be partitioned by left cosets of subgroups whose finite indices are all distinct? Formally: if a finite system of left cosets of subgroups of a group G forms a partition of G, then the finite indices of those subgroups cannot be distinct.
solved_when: A proof, or counterexample, resolving whether such a partition with pairwise distinct finite indices can exist.

title: Dade's conjecture
open: Are the character-theoretic data of blocks of a finite group determined, in Dade's predicted fashion, by the corresponding data of blocks of its local subgroups?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (2026-10-07).
solved_when: Dade's conjectured relations between the numbers of characters of blocks of a finite group and the numbers of characters of blocks of its local subgroups are proved in general (or disproved by counterexample).

title: McKay conjecture
open: Does the number of irreducible complex characters of a finite group G whose degree is not divisible by the prime p equal the number of such characters of the normalizer of a Sylow p-subgroup of G? Formally, for every finite group G and prime p, the McKay conjecture asserts that |Irr_{p′}(G)| = |Irr_{p′}(N_G(P))|, where P is a Sylow p-subgroup of G.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07); source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) establishing, for every finite group G and every prime p, that the number of irreducible complex characters of G of degree not divisible by p equals the number of irreducible complex characters of the normalizer of a Sylow p-subgroup of G.

title: Fuglede's conjecture
open: Which sets in \mathbb{R} and \mathbb{R}^{2} admit an orthogonal basis of exponentials, and is this exactly the same as tiling by translation? Fuglede's conjecture asserts that a (nonconvex) set is spectral if and only if it tiles its ambient space by translations.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07) in the list of unsolved problems in mathematics (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics). No partial results are recorded.
solved_when: The equivalence between spectrality and translational tiling is proved (or disproved, e.g., by an explicit counterexample) for nonconvex sets in \mathbb{R} and \mathbb{R}^{2}; no further quantitative targets are stated in the record.

title: Goodman's conjecture
open: Is Goodman's conjecture on the coefficients of multivalent functions true?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: A proof or disproof of Goodman's conjecture concerning the coefficients of multivalent functions.

title: Superpermutation
open: What is the length of the shortest string on n symbols that contains every permutation of those n symbols as a substring? Formally, determine the minimal length s(n) of a "superpermutation" on n symbols.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (2026-10-07); no further results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A formula or algorithm is established giving the exact minimal length s(n) for all n.

title: Banach's
open: Does there exist an ergodic measure-preserving dynamical system whose spectrum, in the associated unitary-operator sense, is simple Lebesgue spectrum? Equivalently, can a single ergodic transformation generate a unitary operator of countably infinite multiplicity-one Lebesgue type?
status: The problem appears as posed in S. M. Ulam, Problems in Modern Mathematics. Science Editions John Wiley & Sons, Inc., New York, 1964, page 76, and is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: An explicit ergodic measure-preserving dynamical system is constructed (or shown impossible) whose induced unitary operator has simple Lebesgue spectrum.

title: Eden's conjecture
open: Is the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimensions over a global attractor always attained at a stationary point or at an unstable periodic orbit embedded in the attractor?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07); see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for Eden's conjecture: that the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimensions on the global attractor is achieved on a stationary point or an unstable periodic orbit embedded into the attractor.

title: Fatou conjecture
open: Is hyperbolicity generic in the quadratic family — specifically, do the parameters c for which the map z ↦ z² + c is hyperbolic form an open dense subset of the complex plane? Formally, the conjecture asserts that the set of hyperbolic parameters in the quadratic family is open and dense.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the set of parameters c for which z ↦ z² + c is hyperbolic is open and dense in the complex plane.

title: Furstenberg
open: Is every measure on the circle that is invariant and ergodic under the ×2, ×3 action either Lebesgue measure or purely atomic?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing that every invariant ergodic measure for the ×2, ×3 action on the circle is either Lebesgue or atomic; no quantitative targets beyond this dichotomy are stated in the record.

title: Hilbert–Arnold problem
open: Is there a uniform bound on the number of limit cycles in generic finite-parameter families of vector fields on the sphere? More precisely, does there exist a constant, depending only on the number of parameters, that bounds the limit cycles of every generic family with that many parameters?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07). Key reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics
solved_when: A uniform bound on the number of limit cycles is established for generic finite-parameter families of vector fields on the sphere, with the bound depending only on the number of parameters.

title: MLC conjecture
open: Is the Mandelbrot set locally connected? Equivalently, does every point of the Mandelbrot set admit a neighborhood basis of connected sets?
solved_when: A proof, or disproof, that the Mandelbrot set is locally connected at every point.

title: Rokhlin's
open: Are all strongly mixing measure-preserving systems also strongly 3-mixing? That is, does pairwise mixing necessarily extend to mixing of higher orders?
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) is given, for general measure-preserving systems, of the implication from strong mixing to strong 3-mixing.

title: Triangular billiards
open: does every triangle have a periodic billiards path?{{citation

title: Weinstein conjecture
open: Must every regular compact level set of contact type for a Hamiltonian on a symplectic manifold carry at least one periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow? Formally: does the Hamiltonian vector field restricted to such a hypersurface always admit a closed characteristic?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics (as of 2026-10-07). No further state-of-the-art details are given in the record.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) establishing, for every regular compact contact-type level set of a Hamiltonian on a symplectic manifold, whether at least one periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow exists on it.

title: Lyapunov function: Lyapunov's second method for stability
open: For which classes of ordinary differential equations describing dynamical systems does Lyapunov's second method, in its classical and canonically generalized formulations, yield not merely sufficient but necessary and sufficient conditions for (asymptotic) stability of motion? In other words, we seek to characterize exactly when the existence of a Lyapunov function is equivalent to stability.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics (2026-10-07).
solved_when: A characterization is given of the classes of ODEs for which Lyapunov's second method (in classical and canonically generalized forms) provides necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability, with proof of both directions.

title: Bass conjecture
open: Which finitely generated groups have finitely generated algebraic K-groups? More precisely, the Bass conjecture asks whether the algebraic K-groups of suitable group rings arising from finitely generated groups are themselves finitely generated.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) resolving the finite generation of the algebraic K-groups in question for finitely generated groups, as the conjecture is not settled for any stated class of groups in the record.

title: Bass–Quillen conjecture
open: Is every vector bundle over a polynomial ring A[t₁, …, tₙ] over a regular Noetherian ring A extended from a vector bundle over A itself? Formally, the conjecture asks whether the natural pullback map on projective modules K₀(A) → K₀(A[t₁, …, tₙ]) is an isomorphism for every regular Noetherian ring A.
solved_when: The conjecture is resolved affirmatively for all regular Noetherian rings A and all n, i.e., every finitely generated projective module over A[t₁, …, tₙ] is extended from A, or a counterexample is exhibited.

title: Dixmier conjecture
open: Is every endomorphism of the Weyl algebra A₁ also an automorphism — and the same for A₂? Formally, does the Dixmier conjecture hold, i.e., is every endomorphism of the Weyl algebras A_{1} and A_{2} invertible?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every endomorphism of the Weyl algebra A_{1} is an automorphism, and likewise for A_{2}.

title: Fröberg conjecture
open: What are the possible Hilbert functions of a set of homogeneous forms? The Fröberg conjecture predicts that these are exactly the functions given by a certain natural "maximal growth" bound.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia, as of 2026-10-07 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: The conjecture is proved: the Hilbert function of any set of forms coincides with the Fröberg-predicted series (equivalently, every such set of forms achieves maximal growth).

title: General elephant problem
open: Do general elephants — distinguished exceptional divisors arising in birational geometry — have at most Du Val singularities? Formally, is every general elephant on a variety with mild singularities itself a variety whose singularities are at worst Du Val (i.e., rational double points)?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07). Key reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics
solved_when: A proof, or counterexample, establishing whether general elephants always have at most Du Val singularities.

title: Jacobian conjecture
open: If a polynomial map from the plane to itself over a characteristic-0 field has everywhere nonzero constant Jacobian determinant, must it be invertible by a polynomial map? More generally, does a polynomial mapping with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant admit a regular (polynomial-component) inverse?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (accessed 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every two-dimensional polynomial mapping over a characteristic-0 field with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant has a polynomial inverse.

title: Nakai conjecture
open: If the ring of differential operators on a complex algebraic variety is generated by its derivations, must the variety be smooth? Formally, the conjecture predicts that generation of the differential-operator ring by derivations forces the absence of singular points.
status: The conjecture is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07). Key works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing whether every complex algebraic variety whose ring of differential operators is generated by its derivations is smooth.

title: Parshin's conjecture
open: Do the higher algebraic K-groups of every smooth projective variety defined over a finite field vanish up to torsion?
status: The conjecture is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07); see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics.
solved_when: For every smooth projective variety over a finite field, its higher algebraic K-groups are shown to be torsion (i.e., vanish up to torsion); no further quantitative targets are stated.

title: Section conjecture
open: Does every splitting of the natural projection from the étale fundamental group of a smooth, geometrically connected, projective curve over a finitely generated field k onto the absolute Galois group of k arise from a k-rational point of the curve?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07); no further state-of-the-art results are recorded here.
solved_when: For each complete smooth curve over a finitely generated field k, the set of conjugacy classes of splittings of the fundamental-group homomorphism onto Gal(k) is in natural bijection with the set of k-rational points of the curve.

title: Resolution of singularities
open: Does every algebraic variety over a field of characteristic p admit resolution of singularities? More precisely, can the classical characteristic-zero result — that any variety can be transformed by a sequence of blowups into a nonsingular variety — be extended to positive characteristic?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of resolution of singularities for varieties in positive characteristic is given.

title: Borsuk's problem
open: How many pieces of strictly smaller diameter are needed to cover an arbitrary bounded set in n-dimensional Euclidean space? More precisely, what are the sharp upper and lower bounds on the minimum number of smaller-diameter subsets required in such a cover?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics as of 2026-10-07 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: Exact upper and lower bounds are established for the number of smaller-diameter subsets needed to cover any bounded set in n dimensions, for every n.

title: Reinhardt's conjecture
open: Does the smoothed octagon attain the smallest maximum packing density among all centrally-symmetric convex plane sets? That is, is the supremum of packing densities achieved by every centrally-symmetric convex disk in the plane minimized, over this class, by Reinhardt's smoothed octagon?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the smoothed octagon realizes the minimum, over all centrally-symmetric convex plane sets, of their maximum packing density in the plane.

title: Square packing in a square
open: When n unit squares are packed into the smallest possible containing square, how much space must go to waste as n grows? Formally, what is the asymptotic behavior of the wasted area as n → ∞?
solved_when: The asymptotic growth rate of the wasted area for packing n unit squares in a square is determined, matching upper and lower bounds up to constant factors (or exactly).

title: Ulam's packing conjecture
open: about the identity of the worst-packing convex solid

title: Carathéodory conjecture
open: Must every convex, closed, twice-differentiable surface in three-dimensional Euclidean space carry at least two umbilical points? Formally, does such a surface always admit at least two points where the two principal curvatures coincide?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics (as of 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit counterexample) of the existence of at least two umbilical points on every convex, closed, twice-differentiable surface in three-dimensional Euclidean space.

title: Cartan–Hadamard conjecture
open: Does the classical isoperimetric inequality for subsets of Euclidean space extend to Cartan–Hadamard manifolds — complete, simply connected Riemannian manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature? Formally, is the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality the appropriate bound for regions in such spaces?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the extension of the classical isoperimetric inequality to subsets of Hadamard manifolds.

title: Chern's conjecture (affine geometry)
open: that the [[Euler characteristic]] of a [[Closed manifold|compact]] [[affine manifold]] vanishes

title: Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue
open: Is the first eigenvalue of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on an embedded minimal hypersurface of the sphere S^{n+1} equal to n? In other words, does every such minimal hypersurface attain Yau's conjectured lower bound n for its first nonzero eigenvalue?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the first eigenvalue of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on every embedded minimal hypersurface of S^{n+1} equals n.

title: Kalai's 3<sup>''d''</sup> conjecture
open: What is the minimum number of faces a centrally symmetric polytope can have? In particular, is Kalai's conjectured lower bound of 3^d faces attained for every d-dimensional centrally symmetric polytope?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the conjectured lower bound of 3^d on the number of faces of d-dimensional centrally symmetric polytopes.

title: Orchard-planting problem
open: What is the maximum number of lines that can pass through exactly three points in a configuration of n points in the plane? In other words, determine the exact maximum number of 3-point lines attainable by n points, as a function of n.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), on the page "List of unsolved problems in mathematics" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: A formula or sharp characterization of the maximum number of 3-point lines determined by n points is established, resolving the orchard-planting problem for all n.

title: Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem
open: What is the shortest path a swimmer lost in a forest should follow to be certain of reaching the edge? Formally, for a given shape, find the shortest curve that, starting from an unknown point with unknown orientation, is guaranteed to intersect the boundary of the shape.
solved_when: A shortest curve guaranteeing escape is determined for a given shape, with a proof of optimality; the general version of Bellman's problem is resolved when this is settled for all shapes (the classical case being the infinite strip).

title: Ehrhart's volume conjecture
open: Can a convex body in n dimensions whose center of mass is its only interior lattice point have arbitrarily large volume? Formally, is the volume of such a body K always at most (n+1)^n/n!?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (accessed 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the bound: for every convex body K in n dimensions containing a single lattice point in its interior as its center of mass, vol(K) ≤ (n+1)^n/n!.

title: Lebesgue's universal covering problem
open: What is the convex set of least area in the plane that contains a congruent copy of every set of diameter one? Equivalently, determine the exact value of the minimum area of such a universal covering set.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07) in the list of unsolved problems in mathematics (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: The minimum area of a convex universal covering of every planar set of diameter one is determined, with either an explicit optimal set achieving that area or a proof that no smaller covering exists.

title: Mahler's conjecture
open: How small can the product of the volumes of a centrally symmetric convex body and its polar body be? Formally, Mahler's conjecture asserts a sharp lower bound for this volume product among centrally symmetric convex bodies.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the conjectured sharp lower bound on the volume product of a centrally symmetric convex body and its polar is established.

title: Shephard's problem (a.k.a. Dürer's conjecture)
open: Does every convex polyhedron admit a net — that is, can its surface be cut along edges and unfolded into a single non-overlapping polygon in the plane?
status: The problem, also known as Dürer's conjecture, is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics, as of 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) establishing whether every convex polyhedron has an edge-unfolding that produces a simple net, with no pair of faces overlapping in the plane.

title: Hilbert's third problem
open: for non-Euclidean geometries: in spherical or hyperbolic geometry, must polyhedra with the same volume and [[Dehn invariant]] be scissors-congruent?

title: Brouwer's conjecture
open: Is there a sharp upper bound on the sum of the largest eigenvalues of the Laplacian matrix of a graph in terms of the graph's number of edges? Formally, the question asks whether the sum of the largest Laplacian eigenvalues of a graph is bounded above by a function of the number of edges (as conjectured by Brouwer).
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07); see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of Brouwer's conjectured upper bound on sums of Laplacian eigenvalues in terms of the number of edges is established.

title: Graham's pebbling conjecture
open: Is Graham's pebbling conjecture true — that is, does the pebbling number of a Cartesian product of graphs satisfy the expected bound in terms of the pebbling numbers of the factors?
status: The problem appears as an entry on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics, listed as unsolved as of 2026-10-07.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the conjectured bound on the pebbling number of Cartesian products of graphs.

title: Cereceda's conjecture
open: How large can the diameter of the solution graph be for recoloring a degenerate graph? More precisely, is Cereceda's conjecture true — does the space of proper colorings of any degenerate graph admit the conjectured quadratic (in the number of vertices) bound on its diameter under single-vertex recoloring steps?
status: The problem appears on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics as of 2026-10-07, with no further partial results stated in the record. Key work: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of Cereceda's conjecture on the diameter of the space of colorings of degenerate graphs; the record states no further quantitative targets.

title: Jaeger's Petersen-coloring conjecture
open: Does every bridgeless cubic graph admit a cycle-continuous mapping to the Petersen graph? Formally, is there always a homomorphism that sends cycles to cycles between such a graph and the Petersen graph?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing that every bridgeless cubic graph does, or does not, have a cycle-continuous mapping to the Petersen graph.

title: Harborth's conjecture
open: Can every planar graph be drawn in the plane so that all of its edges have integer lengths? Equivalently, does every planar graph admit a planar straight-line embedding in which each edge is a segment of integer Euclidean length?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every planar graph has a plane straight-line drawing with all edge lengths integers; a single planar graph shown to admit no such drawing would resolve the conjecture negatively.

title: Turán's brick factory problem
open: Is there a drawing of any complete bipartite graph with fewer crossings than the number given by Zarankiewicz? That is, does the Zarankiewicz formula fail to give the true crossing number of some complete bipartite graph?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: A drawing of some complete bipartite graph is exhibited whose number of crossings is strictly smaller than the Zarankiewicz bound, or the Zarankiewicz formula is proven to always equal the crossing number.

title: Conway's 99-graph problem
open: Does there exist a strongly regular graph with parameters (99,14,1,2)? More precisely, is there a 99-vertex graph in which every vertex has 14 neighbors, adjacent vertices share exactly 1 common neighbor, and non-adjacent vertices share exactly 2?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: Either a strongly regular graph with parameters (99,14,1,2) is explicitly constructed, or it is proved that no such graph exists.

title: Degree diameter problem
open: Given a maximum degree d and a diameter k, how many vertices can a graph have? Formally, determine (or sharply bound) the largest order n(d, k) of a graph with maximum degree at most d and diameter at most k.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07).
solved_when: Exact values of n(d, k), or asymptotically tight bounds on n(d, k), are known for all positive integers d and k.

title: Barnette's conjecture
open: Does every cubic, bipartite, three-connected planar graph contain a Hamiltonian cycle? In other words, is every such graph — the class known as Barnette graphs — Hamiltonian?
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) resolving whether every cubic bipartite three-connected planar graph admits a Hamiltonian cycle.

title: Gilbert–Pollak conjecture
open: Is the Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane exactly √3/2, as conjectured by Gilbert and Pollak? Formally, is the supremum over all finite point sets in the plane of the ratio of the length of a minimum spanning tree to the length of a shortest Steiner tree equal to √3/2?
solved_when: The conjecture is settled by a proof (or disproof) that the Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane equals √3/2 — that is, no finite point set in the Euclidean plane has ratio exceeding √3/2, and examples attaining √3/2 (such as the vertices of an equilateral triangle) establish the value.

title: Sumner's conjecture
open: does every (2n-2)-vertex tournament contain as a subgraph every n-vertex oriented tree?{{citation

title: Szymanski's conjecture
open: Can every permutation of the vertices of an n-dimensional doubly-directed hypercube graph be routed along edge-disjoint paths? That is, for any permutation on the vertices of the directed hypercube Q_n, do there exist pairwise edge-disjoint directed paths connecting each source to its designated target?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07 (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that edge-disjoint routing exists for every permutation on the n-dimensional doubly-directed hypercube for every n; equivalently, an explicit permutation and dimension n for which no such routing exists would resolve the conjecture negatively.

title: Tuza's conjecture
open: If a graph contains at most ν pairwise edge-disjoint triangles, is there always a set of at most 2ν edges that meets every triangle? Equivalently, writing τ for the minimum size of a set of edges hitting all triangles, Tuza's conjecture asks whether τ ≤ 2ν holds in every graph.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of the inequality τ ≤ 2ν for all graphs, where ν is the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles and τ is the minimum size of an edge set intersecting every triangle.

title: Vizing's conjecture
open: Is the domination number of a cartesian product of graphs always at least the product of the domination numbers of the factors — that is, does γ(G □ H) ≥ γ(G)γ(H) hold for all graphs G and H?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of the inequality γ(G □ H) ≥ γ(G)γ(H) for all pairs of finite graphs.

title: Walescki's theorem for hypergraphs
open: Do complete k-uniform hypergraphs admit Hamiltonian decompositions into tight cycles?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every complete k-uniform hypergraph decomposes into tight Hamiltonian cycles.

title: Ryser's conjecture
open: In an $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraph, must the minimum size of a transversal (vertex cover) be at most $(r-1)$ times the maximum matching size? The conjecture asserts that this $(r-1)$ factor is the worst case for the natural relaxation of König's theorem to hypergraphs.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof or counterexample is given for the bound $\tau \le (r-1)\nu$ in $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraphs, resolving the conjecture for all $r$.

title: Woodall's conjecture
open: In any directed graph, is the minimum number of edges in a dicut equal to the maximum number of pairwise disjoint dijoins? Formally, the conjecture asserts a min–max equality between the minimum size of a dicut and the maximum number of disjoint dijoins.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that for every directed graph, the minimum number of edges in a dicut equals the maximum number of disjoint dijoins.

title: Tarski's exponential function problem
open: Is the first-order theory of the real numbers together with the exponential function decidable? Formally: is there an algorithm that decides whether any given first-order sentence in the language of ordered rings augmented by the exponential function holds over the reals?
status: The problem originates with Tarski and remains open; it is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (as of 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A decision procedure is exhibited that, for every first-order sentence in the language of ordered fields with exponentiation, determines whether it is true over the real numbers — or the theory is proved undecidable.

title: Büchi's problem
open: Must a sufficiently long sequence of square numbers with constant second difference be forced into the trivial pattern? Formally, is there a finite length beyond which any integer square sequence with constant second difference is necessarily trivial?
solved_when: An explicit bound M is established such that every sequence of M square numbers with constant second difference is trivial, or a counterexample of arbitrary length is produced.

title: Carmichael's totient function conjecture
open: Does every value of Euler's totient function occur with multiplicity greater than 1 — that is, is no integer m the value φ(n) for exactly one n? Formally, for every n, does there exist m ≠ n with φ(m) = φ(n)?
solved_when: A proof that for every n there is some m ≠ n with φ(m) = φ(n); equivalently, a disproof would be an explicit n with φ(n) = φ(m) for no other m.

title: Catalan–Dickson conjecture on aliquot sequences
open: Is every aliquot sequence eventually periodic or terminating? Formally, the Catalan–Dickson conjecture asserts that no aliquot sequence is infinite yet never repeats.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of whether every aliquot sequence — obtained by iterating the sum-of-proper-divisors function — eventually reaches a prime, enters a cycle (such as a perfect or amicable pair), or is shown to continue indefinitely without repetition.

title: Exponent pair conjecture
open: Is \((\varepsilon,\,1/2+\varepsilon)\) an exponent pair for every \(\varepsilon > 0\)? That is, does this conjectured pair satisfy the defining closure properties of exponent pairs, yielding essentially optimal estimates in the theory of exponential sums?
solved_when: A proof that for all \(\varepsilon > 0\) the pair \((\varepsilon,\,1/2+\varepsilon)\) is an exponent pair (or a disproof via a counterexample for some \(\varepsilon\)).

title: Grimm's conjecture
open: Given any run of consecutive composite numbers, is it always possible to assign to each number in the run a distinct prime divisor of that number? Formally: for every set of consecutive composite integers, there exists a matching between the elements and distinct primes such that each prime divides its assigned element.
status: The conjecture is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07. Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every finite run of consecutive composite numbers admits such an assignment of distinct prime divisors.

title: Hall's conjecture
open: How close can a perfect square and a perfect cube be to each other? Formally, Hall's conjecture asks whether, for every ε > 0, there exists a constant c(ε) > 0 such that for all integers x, y with y² ≠ x³, we have |y² − x³| > c(ε)·x^(1/2 − ε).
status: The problem appears on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics (accessed 2026-10-07) and remains open.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the statement: for any ε > 0 there is a constant c(ε) such that either y² = x³ or |y² − x³| > c(ε)x^(1/2 − ε).

title: Magic square of squares
open: is there a 3x3 magic square composed of distinct perfect squares?

title: Mahler's 3/2 problem
open: Does there exist a real number x such that the fractional parts of x(3/2)^n all lie below 1/2, for every positive integer n? In other words, is Mahler's conjecture true that no such x exists?
solved_when: A proof that no real number x satisfies {x(3/2)^n} < 1/2 for all positive integers n — or an explicit example of such an x.

title: Scholz conjecture
open: Is the shortest addition chain for 2^n − 1 never longer than the chain for n shifted by n − 1 steps? Formally, is ℓ(2^n − 1) ≤ ℓ(n) + n − 1, where ℓ(m) denotes the length of the shortest addition chain producing m?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics (as of 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the inequality ℓ(2^n − 1) ≤ ℓ(n) + n − 1 for all positive integers n.

title: Singmaster's conjecture
open: Is there a finite constant that bounds how many times any integer greater than 1 can appear in Pascal's triangle? Formally, does there exist a constant C such that no entry of Pascal's triangle exceeding 1 occurs more than C times?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: A finite upper bound C is proven for the multiplicities of all entries greater than 1 in Pascal's triangle; alternatively, the conjecture is refuted by exhibiting an integer greater than 1 appearing arbitrarily many times.

title: Erdős–Turán conjecture on additive bases
open: If a set B of nonnegative integers is an additive basis of order 2 — so that every sufficiently large positive integer is a sum of two elements of B — must the number of representations of n as such a sum tend to infinity as n tends to infinity?
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, is given for the statement that for every additive basis B of order 2, the representation function r_{B,2}(n) → ∞ as n → ∞.

title: Lemoine's conjecture
open: Can every odd integer greater than 5 be represented as the sum of an odd prime and an even semiprime?
status: The conjecture is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every odd integer greater than 5 is the sum of an odd prime and an even semiprime; a counterexample suffices to resolve it negatively.

title: Skolem problem
open: Is there an algorithm that, given a constant-recursive (linearly recurrent) sequence, decides whether it contains a zero? Equivalently, for an integer linear recurrence, can the existence of some index n with u_n = 0 be decided in finite time?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07). Key reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics
solved_when: An explicit decision procedure (or a proof that none exists) for determining whether an arbitrary constant-recursive sequence attains the value zero.

title: Hermite's problem
open: Is there, for each natural number n, a way of assigning a sequence of natural numbers to every real number so that the sequence assigned to x is eventually periodic exactly when x is algebraic of degree n?
solved_when: For every natural number n, such an assignment of natural-number sequences to the reals exists, with eventual periodicity characterizing exactly the algebraic numbers of degree n; a negative answer for some n also resolves the problem.

title: Kummer–Vandiver conjecture
open: Does every prime p fail to divide the class number of the maximal real subfield of the p-th cyclotomic field? Equivalently, is the class number of ℚ(ζₚ)⁺ never divisible by p?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07). No year, author results, or bounds are stated in the record.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that for every prime p, p does not divide the class number of the maximal real subfield of the p-th cyclotomic field; a single prime p dividing that class number would resolve it negatively.

title: Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture
open: Do the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, when properly normalized, exhibit the same pair correlations as eigenvalues of random Hermitian matrices from the Gaussian ensembles? Formally, Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture asserts that the normalized pair correlation function between pairs of zeros of the Riemann zeta function equals the pair correlation function of random Hermitian matrices.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07). Key reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics
solved_when: The conjecture is resolved by a proof (or disproof) that the normalized pair correlation function of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function coincides with the pair correlation function of random Hermitian matrices from the Gaussian ensembles.

title: Piltz divisor problem
open: How large can the error term Δ_k(x) = D_k(x) − xP_k(log x) be, where D_k(x) counts integers up to x with exactly k divisors and P_k is the associated approximating polynomial? More precisely, the problem asks for sharp bounds on the growth of this error term as x → ∞.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics), as of 2026-10-07.
solved_when: An asymptotically sharp bound on Δ_k(x) is established; since the record states no explicit exponent target, the natural criterion is a proof matching the conjectured optimal order of the error term for general k.

title: Selberg's 1/4 conjecture
open: Are the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator on Maass wave forms of congruence subgroups always at least 1/4? Formally, Selberg's 1/4 conjecture asserts a sharp lower bound of 1/4 for the (suitably normalized) Laplacian eigenvalues in this setting.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics (as of 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof that every such eigenvalue is at least 1/4, or a counterexample exhibiting one below 1/4.

title: Selberg's orthogonality conjecture
open: Does a Mertens-type theorem — an analogue of the second Mertens theorem on the asymptotics of summed arithmetic functions — hold for functions belonging to the Selberg class? More precisely, can the classical statement be generalized to this class of Dirichlet series?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (as of 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the generalized Mertens-type asymptotic for functions in the Selberg class is established.

title: Erdős–Ulam problem
open: Is there a dense set of points in the plane such that every pair of points is at a rational distance from one another?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), per the list of unsolved problems in mathematics (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: A construction of such a dense, pairwise rational-distance set is exhibited, or a proof is given that no such set exists.

title: Zilber–Pink conjecture
open: If X is a mixed Shimura variety or semiabelian variety over \mathbb{C} and V ⊆ X is a subvariety, must V contain only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties? Formally, the conjecture asserts that such a V has only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07); no further state-of-the-art results are given in the record.
solved_when: The conjecture is proved, or disproved, for mixed Shimura varieties and semiabelian varieties over \mathbb{C}: namely, that every subvariety V of such an X contains only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties.

title: Littlewood conjecture
open: Is it true that for every pair of real numbers \alpha and \beta, the product n\Vert n\alpha\Vert\Vert n\beta\Vert gets arbitrarily close to zero along a sequence of integers n, where \Vert x\Vert denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer? Formally, does \liminf_{n \rightarrow \infty} n\,\Vert n\alpha\Vert\,\Vert n\beta\Vert = 0 hold for all real \alpha, \beta?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), in its list of unsolved problems in mathematics (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the stated limit inferior equals zero for every pair of real numbers \alpha, \beta; a single explicit counterexample pair would resolve it negatively.

title: Beal's conjecture
open: Must every solution in positive integers of A^x + B^y = C^z with all exponents x, y, z greater than 2 have A, B, C sharing a common prime factor? Equivalently, is there no solution with A, B, C pairwise coprime?
solved_when: A proof or counterexample is given for the assertion that every integer solution of A^x + B^y = C^z with x, y, z > 2 has a prime dividing all of A, B, and C.

title: Brocard's problem
open: Are there any integer solutions to n! + 1 = m² beyond the known cases n = 4, 5, 7, or are these the only ones?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: Either a new integer solution (n, m) with n ∉ {4, 5, 7} is exhibited, or it is proved that no further integer solutions exist.

title: Congruent number problem
open: Which rational numbers are congruent numbers — that is, which arise as the area of a right triangle with rational side lengths? The goal is a complete, effective characterization of the set of congruent numbers.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), as a corollary to the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, per Tunnell's theorem; the goal is to determine precisely what rational numbers are congruent numbers. Key work: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics
solved_when: An explicit criterion is given that determines, for any rational number, whether it is congruent; a full proof of the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture would yield such a criterion (via Tunnell's theorem).

title: Goormaghtigh conjecture
open: When can two different repunits in different bases coincide — that is, when does (x^m − 1)/(x − 1) = (y^n − 1)/(y − 1) with x > y > 1 and m, n > 2? The Goormaghtigh conjecture asks for a complete description of all such integer solutions.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics); no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: All integer solutions to (x^m − 1)/(x − 1) = (y^n − 1)/(y − 1) with x > y > 1 and m, n > 2 are determined, and the conjectured finiteness (the expected small set of solutions) is proved.

title: Pillai's conjecture
open: Given fixed nonzero integers A, B, and C, can the exponential Diophantine equation Ax^m − By^n = C have infinitely many solutions in positive integers? Pillai's conjecture asserts that it cannot, provided the exponents m and n are not both equal to 2.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that for every choice of A, B, C the equation Ax^m − By^n = C has only finitely many solutions whenever m and n are not both 2.

title: Agoh–Giuga conjecture
open: Is there a characterization of primality through Bernoulli numbers, namely: is every positive integer p prime exactly when pB_{p-1} ≡ -1 (mod p)? Equivalently, must every composite n satisfying nB_{n-1} ≡ -1 (mod n) — a Giuga number — actually fail to exist?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics.
solved_when: A proof or disproof of the equivalence "p is prime if and only if pB_{p-1} ≡ -1 (mod p)" for all positive integers p; in particular, either a proof that no composite n satisfies the congruence, or an explicit composite counterexample.

title: Agrawal's conjecture
open: Is it true that for coprime positive integers n and r, whenever the congruence (X − 1)^n ≡ X^n − 1 holds modulo n and X^r − 1, then n must be prime or satisfy n² ≡ 1 (mod r)?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07.
solved_when: A proof or a counterexample is given: either the implication is established for all coprime positive integers n and r, or specific n, r are exhibited with (X − 1)^n ≡ X^n − 1 (mod n, X^r − 1) while n is composite and n² ≢ 1 (mod r).

title: Artin's conjecture on primitive roots
open: If an integer is neither a perfect square nor -1, must it be a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes?
solved_when: For every integer that is neither a perfect square nor -1, it is shown to be a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes.

title: Brocard's conjecture
open: Are there always at least 4 primes strictly between the squares of two consecutive primes, apart from the single exception between 2² and 3²?
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit counterexample) of the claim that for every pair of consecutive primes p < q other than 2 and 3, the open interval (p², q²) contains at least 4 primes.

title: Bunyakovsky conjecture
open: If an integer-coefficient polynomial is irreducible over the integers, has a positive leading coefficient, and its values share no common factor, must it take prime values infinitely often?
status: The conjecture is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the general statement: any such polynomial f(x) is prime for infinitely many positive integers x.

title: Dickson's conjecture
open: Given finitely many linear forms a_1 + b_1 n, …, a_k + b_k n with each b_i ≥ 1, must there be infinitely many n for which every one of the forms is simultaneously prime, unless some congruence obstruction prevents it?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) of the assertion: for any finite set of such linear forms, either infinitely many n make all forms prime, or there exists a congruence condition demonstrably ruling out all such n.

title: Erdős–Mollin–Walsh conjecture
open: Can three consecutive integers all be powerful, meaning each is divisible by the square of every prime that divides it? The Erdős–Mollin–Walsh conjecture asserts that no such triple exists.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07.
solved_when: A proof that no three consecutive integers are all powerful, or an explicit counterexample exhibiting such a triple.

title: Feit–Thompson conjecture
open: If p and q are distinct primes, can the cyclotomic value (p^q − 1)/(p − 1) divide (q^p − 1)/(q − 1)? The Feit–Thompson conjecture asserts that this never happens for any pair of distinct primes.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07.
solved_when: A proof that for all distinct primes p and q, (p^q − 1)/(p − 1) does not divide (q^p − 1)/(q − 1); or a counterexample exhibiting a pair of distinct primes for which the divisibility holds.

title: New Mersenne conjecture
open: For any odd natural number p, if any two of the three conditions — p = 2^k ± 1 or p = 4^k ± 3, 2^p − 1 prime, and (2^p + 1)/3 prime — hold, must the third also hold?
status: The problem appears on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07) and remains open. Key reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics
solved_when: The implication is proved for all odd natural numbers p, or a counterexample p is exhibited for which exactly two of the three conditions hold.

title: Polignac's conjecture
open: Does every positive even number occur as the size of infinitely many prime gaps? Formally, for every even n, are there infinitely many pairs of consecutive primes p, p+n?
solved_when: For every positive even number n, it is proved that infinitely many consecutive prime pairs differ by exactly n.

title: Selfridge's conjecture
open: is 78,557 the lowest [[Sierpiński number]]?

title: Siegel's conjecture
open: Are there infinitely many regular primes, and if so, do they have a natural density of e^{-1/2} among all primes?
solved_when: It is proved that regular primes are infinite in number; and, further, that their natural density within the primes exists and equals e^{-1/2} (or is shown to equal some other value).

title: Reinhardt cardinal
open: Without assuming the axiom of choice, can there exist a nontrivial elementary embedding from the universe V into itself — that is, a Reinhardt cardinal? In formal terms, is the existence of such an embedding consistent with ZF alone?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07). Key work: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics
solved_when: A proof or disproof (in ZF, without choice) of the consistency of a nontrivial elementary embedding V→V is given.

title: Berge conjecture
open: Which knots in the 3-sphere admit a Dehn surgery yielding a lens space? The conjecture asserts that the only such knots are Berge knots.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation with a counterexample) that a knot in the 3-sphere admits a lens space Dehn surgery if and only if it is a Berge knot.

title: Bing–Borsuk conjecture
open: Must every homogeneous absolute neighborhood retract (ANR) of dimension n be a topological manifold? Formally, the conjecture asserts that every n-dimensional homogeneous ANR is homeomorphic to an n-manifold.
solved_when: A proof, or counterexample, is given for the statement that every n-dimensional homogeneous absolute neighborhood retract is a topological manifold.

title: Borel conjecture
open: [[Aspherical space|aspherical]] and [[closed manifold]]s are determined up to [[homeomorphism]] by their [[fundamental group]]s

title: Hilbert–Smith conjecture
open: Must every locally compact topological group that acts continuously and faithfully on a topological manifold be a Lie group? This is the Hilbert–Smith conjecture, which asks whether such a faithful action forces the acting group to have a compatible smooth structure.
status: The conjecture is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every locally compact topological group with a continuous, faithful action on a topological manifold is a Lie group.

title: Whitehead conjecture
open: Is every connected subcomplex of a two-dimensional aspherical CW complex itself aspherical?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) establishing whether every connected subcomplex of a two-dimensional aspherical CW complex is aspherical.

title: Zeeman conjecture
open: If K is a finite contractible two-dimensional CW complex, is the product K × [0, 1] collapsible?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), in the list of unsolved problems in mathematics. No partial resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given that for every finite contractible 2-dimensional CW complex K, the product K × [0, 1] is collapsible, or an explicit counterexample is constructed.

title: Mazur's conjecture B
open: Is Mazur's conjecture B true? The record gives no formal statement of the conjecture beyond its name.
status: The conjecture is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (as of 2026-10-07); work by Vessilin Dimitrov, Ziyang Gao, and Philipp Habegger (2020) is associated with it, per the record.
solved_when: A proof or disproof of Mazur's conjecture B is established.

title: Eremenko's
open: Is every component of the escaping set of an entire transcendental function unbounded? That is, must each connected component of $I(f) = \{z : f^n(z) \to \infty\}$ be unbounded?
status: The conjecture is attributed to David Martí-Pete, Lasse Rempe, and James Waterman (2025) and remains listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026-10-07.
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, showing that every component of the escaping set of every entire transcendental function is unbounded (or that some component of some such function is bounded).

title: Ringel's conjecture
open: Can the complete graph K_{2n+1} always be decomposed into 2n+1 copies of any tree with n edges?
status: The conjecture is attributed to work of Richard Montgomery, Benny Sudakov, and Alexey Pokrovskiy (2020), and it is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (as of 2026-10-07).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for every n: an explicit decomposition of K_{2n+1} into 2n+1 edge-disjoint copies of an arbitrary n-edge tree, or a specific n and tree for which no such decomposition exists.

title: Alexandre Eremenko
open: Which problems of function theory collected on Alexandre Eremenko's unsolved problems page remain open, and can any of them be resolved?
solved_when: A problem listed on Eremenko's page (https://www.math.purdue.edu/~eremenko/uns1.html) is resolved, or shown equivalent to a known settled question.

title: Boundedness of elliptic-curve ranks over \(\mathbb Q\)
open: Is there an absolute constant bounding the rank of every elliptic curve over \(\mathbb Q\)? Either prove such a universal bound exists, or construct elliptic curves over \(\mathbb Q\) of arbitrarily large rank.
status: Open since the twentieth-century development of Mordell–Weil theory. Dujella's maintained table records rank at least 31 by Alpöge–Howell in 2026; finite records cannot resolve boundedness. Heuristics suggesting boundedness appear in Jennifer Park, Bjorn Poonen, John Voight and Melanie Matchett Wood (2019), *A heuristic for boundedness of ranks of elliptic curves*, [arXiv:1602.01431](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.01431).
solved_when: Either an absolute constant \(B\) is proven such that every elliptic curve over \(\mathbb Q\) has rank at most \(B\), or an infinite family of elliptic curves over \(\mathbb Q\) is constructed whose ranks grow without bound.
why: A solution determines whether the rational-point groups of elliptic curves can have arbitrarily complex structure or are globally constrained, resolving a basic structural question about Mordell–Weil groups over \(\mathbb Q\).
key_works: Andrej Dujella, [*History of elliptic curves rank records*](https://web.math.pmf.unizg.hr/~duje/tors/rankhist.html); Jennifer Park, Bjorn Poonen, John Voight and Melanie Matchett Wood (2019), *A heuristic for boundedness of ranks of elliptic curves*, [arXiv:1602.01431](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.01431).

title: Termination of flips
open: Does the basic operation of the minimal model program ever run forever? Formally, prove that every sequence of \((K_X+\Delta)\)-flips starting from a projective \(\mathbb Q\)-factorial Kawamata log terminal characteristic-zero pair has finite length.
status: A central question dating to the 1980s. Termination is known in dimension three and in substantial higher-dimensional cases; note that existence of flips does not by itself guarantee termination. Background: Kollár and Mori (1998), *Birational Geometry of Algebraic Varieties*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511662560); Caucher Birkar (2018), *Birational geometry of algebraic varieties*, [arXiv:1801.00013](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.00013).
solved_when: A proof shows that any such flip sequence terminates after finitely many steps.
why: It would ensure that a basic operation of the minimal model program cannot continue indefinitely, so the program reliably reaches an output.
key_works: Kollár and Mori (1998), *Birational Geometry of Algebraic Varieties*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511662560); Caucher Birkar (2018), *Birational geometry of algebraic varieties*, [arXiv:1801.00013](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.00013).

title: Complex structure on the six-sphere
open: Does the smooth six-sphere \(S^6\) admit a genuine complex structure — that is, is there an integrable almost-complex structure on it? A resolution would either construct an explicit complex atlas or prove that none can exist.
status: Open since the mid-twentieth century. Almost-complex structures on \(S^6\) exist, but the standard octonionic structure is not integrable; any complex structure would necessarily be non-Kähler. Christian Lehn, Sönke Rollenske and Caren Schinko (2018), *The complex geometry of a hypothetical complex structure on S6*, [arXiv:1912.09719](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.09719), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.difgeo.2017.10.015).
solved_when: Either an integrable almost-complex structure (complex atlas) on \(S^6\) is constructed, or it is proved that no such structure exists.
why: It would settle the basic boundary between almost-complex and complex geometry on spheres: almost-complex structures exist on \(S^6\), yet whether integrability is attainable remains unknown.
key_works: Christian Lehn, Sönke Rollenske and Caren Schinko (2018), *The complex geometry of a hypothetical complex structure on S6*, [arXiv:1912.09719](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.09719), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.difgeo.2017.10.015).

title: Ribbon status of the knot 18_nh00000601
open: Is the eighteen-crossing knot \(18_{\mathrm{nh}00000601}\) actually a ribbon knot? It is known to be smoothly slice in the standard four-ball, so any valid obstruction to its being ribbon would disprove the slice–ribbon conjecture.
status: The knot became a concrete target in 2026. Trevor Oliveira-Smith (2026), *A Dunfield–Gong 4-Sphere is Standard*, [arXiv:2603.23717](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23717), proved that it bounds a fibered handle-ribbon disk; handle-ribbon is weaker than ribbon.
solved_when: A proof that \(18_{\mathrm{nh}00000601}\) is ribbon, or a proof that it is not ribbon (which would disprove slice–ribbon).
why: It supplies a specific finite knot whose ribbon classification could resolve the slice–ribbon conjecture.

title: Global Langlands functoriality
status: Proposed in 1967. Base change, classical-group transfers, several tensor products, and holomorphic symmetric powers are major successes; arbitrary groups and homomorphisms remain open. James Arthur (2021), *An Introduction to Langlands Functoriality*, [manuscript](https://www.math.toronto.edu/arthur/pdf/Introduction_to_Langlands_Functoriality_June29.pdf), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1017/9781108591218.016); Jae-Hyun Yang (2008), *Langlands Functoriality Conjecture*, [arXiv:0808.0917](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.0917).
solved_when: For every such pair of groups and every admissible \(L\)-homomorphism, the transfer of automorphic representations with compatible unramified Satake parameters is constructed.
why: A solution would organize automorphic forms across groups through a common system of transfer principles.
key_works: James Arthur (2021), *An Introduction to Langlands Functoriality*, [manuscript](https://www.math.toronto.edu/arthur/pdf/Introduction_to_Langlands_Functoriality_June29.pdf), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1017/9781108591218.016); Jae-Hyun Yang (2008), *Langlands Functoriality Conjecture*, [arXiv:0808.0917](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.0917).

title: Symmetric-power functoriality for Maass forms
open: For every cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_2/\mathbb Q\) arising from a Hecke–Maass form and every \(m\ge1\), does the predicted automorphic symmetric-power transfer to \(\mathrm{GL}_{m+1}\) exist? Formally, the task is to construct this Langlands transfer unconditionally for arbitrary Maass forms.
status: The problem has been part of the Langlands program since the 1960s–1970s. Low symmetric powers are known, and Newton–Thorne proved symmetric power functoriality for all powers for holomorphic modular forms (James Newton and Jack Thorne (2021), *Symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic modular forms, II*, [arXiv:2009.07180](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.07180); see also Newton (2022), *Modularity of Galois Representations and Langlands Functoriality*, [survey](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/newton/iisc.pdf)), but this does not settle the case of arbitrary Maass forms.
solved_when: The symmetric-power lifting from every Hecke–Maass cuspidal representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_2/\mathbb Q\) to \(\mathrm{GL}_{m+1}\) is constructed for every integer \(m\ge1\).
why: It would extend analytic continuation and representation-theoretic control to all symmetric-power \(L\)-functions of Maass forms, closing the Maass-form gap in the Langlands functoriality picture.
key_works: James Newton and Jack Thorne (2021), *Symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic modular forms, II*, [arXiv:2009.07180](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.07180); Newton (2022), *Modularity of Galois Representations and Langlands Functoriality*, [survey](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/newton/iisc.pdf).

title: Symplectic isotopy of smooth plane curves in degree at least eighteen
open: Is every connected smooth symplectic degree-\(d\) surface in \(\mathbb{CP}^2\) symplectically isotopic to a complex algebraic curve? In other words, do smooth symplectic plane curves of sufficiently high degree exhibit any flexibility beyond that of their algebraic counterparts?
status: The problem developed after Gromov's 1985 work. Current results cover degrees through seventeen; the general case remains unresolved beginning at degree eighteen. Key works include Bernd Siebert and Gang Tian (2005), *On the holomorphicity of genus two Lefschetz fibrations*, and Laura Starkston (2017), *A new approach to the symplectic isotopy problem*, [arXiv:1709.02544](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.02544).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) settles symplectic isotopy to a complex algebraic curve for every connected smooth symplectic surface in \(\mathbb{CP}^2\) of degree at least eighteen, or exhibits such a surface not isotopic to any algebraic curve.
why: A solution would determine whether symplectic plane curves possess flexibility absent from algebraic curves, separating the symplectic and complex-algebraic categories in dimension four.
key_works: Bernd Siebert and Gang Tian (2005), *On the holomorphicity of genus two Lefschetz fibrations*; Laura Starkston (2017), *A new approach to the symplectic isotopy problem*, [arXiv:1709.02544](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.02544).

title: Transcendence of Catalan’s constant
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Is Catalan’s constant \(G=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n/(2n+1)^2\) transcendental? Even a rigorous proof of irrationality would itself be substantial progress.
status: The constant dates to the nineteenth century. Transcendence remains unresolved. A September 2026 irrationality claim by Zhi-Wei Sun (2026), *Catalan’s constant is irrational*, [arXiv:2609.04176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04176), was challenged by exact computations in a subsequent preprint, Dane Wachs (2026), *A note on a recent claimed proof of the irrationality of Catalan’s constant*, [arXiv:2609.22339](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22339). Related foundational work: Yu. V. Nesterenko (2016), *On Catalan’s constant*, [DOI:10.1134/S0081543816010107](https://doi.org/10.1134/S0081543816010107).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that \(G\) is transcendental; an accepted proof of irrationality alone counts as major partial progress.
why: It isolates a special \(L\)-value whose arithmetic nature lies beyond established methods of transcendence theory and Diophantine approximation.
key_works: Yu. V. Nesterenko (2016), *On Catalan’s constant*, [DOI:10.1134/S0081543816010107](https://doi.org/10.1134/S0081543816010107); Zhi-Wei Sun (2026), *Catalan’s constant is irrational*, [arXiv:2609.04176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04176), challenged claim; Dane Wachs (2026), *A note on a recent claimed proof of the irrationality of Catalan’s constant*, [arXiv:2609.22339](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22339).

title: Lehmer’s Mahler-measure problem
subfield: Transcendental number theory and Diophantine approximation
open: Is there a universal constant \(c>1\) such that every nonzero algebraic integer that is not a root of unity has Mahler measure at least \(c\)? The conjectured optimal value is Lehmer's number, approximately 1.17628.
status: The problem was asked in 1933. Dobrowolski's degree-dependent lower bounds approach one, and nonreciprocal polynomials are known to admit a uniform gap. See Chris Smyth (2008), *The Mahler measure of algebraic numbers: a survey*, [arXiv:math/0701397](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701397), [manuscript](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~chris/papers/Smyth240707.pdf).
solved_when: A constant \(c>1\) is exhibited (and proved) as a uniform lower bound for the Mahler measure of every nonzero algebraic integer that is not a root of unity; the conjectural optimum is \(c \approx 1.17628\), Lehmer's number.
why: A solution would establish a universal arithmetic gap above the smallest possible Mahler measure, separating non-cyclotomic algebraic integers from roots of unity in a quantitative way.
key_works: Chris Smyth (2008), *The Mahler measure of algebraic numbers: a survey*, [arXiv:math/0701397](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701397), [manuscript](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~chris/papers/Smyth240707.pdf).

title: Finite lattice representation problem
open: Is every finite lattice isomorphic to the congruence lattice of some finite algebra? In other words, does every finite lattice arise as the lattice of congruences of a finite universal algebra?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), in its list of unsolved problems in mathematics.
