solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) showing that every finite lattice is, or is not, isomorphic to the congruence lattice of some finite algebra; any construction must produce a finite algebra for each finite lattice.

title: Hilbert's sixteenth problem
open: What configurations of connected components can an M-curve realize? More precisely, which arrangements of the ovals of a real algebraic curve of degree d with the maximal number of components permitted by Harnack's curve theorem actually occur?
solved_when: A complete characterization of the possible oval configurations of M-curves of each degree is given, together with a proof that no other configurations arise.

title: No-three-in-line problem
open: How many points can be placed on an \(n \times n\) grid so that no three of them lie on a single straight line?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: An explicit formula, or sharp asymptotics, is determined for the maximum number of such points as a function of \(n\).

title: Birkhoff
open: If a billiard table is strictly convex and its billiard flow is integrable, must the boundary of the table be an ellipse? Equivalently, is the ellipse the only strictly convex curve whose interior billiard dynamics admits a complete set of conserved quantities?
status: Listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07); see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given: either every strictly convex, integrable billiard table has elliptical boundary, or a strictly convex non-elliptical table with integrable billiard dynamics is constructed.

title: Sphere packing
open: What is the maximum density of a packing of congruent spheres in Euclidean space in dimensions other than 1, 2, 3, 8, and 24, and how does this density behave asymptotically as the dimension grows? Formally, determine the exact densest-packing density in each open dimension and characterize its high-dimensional asymptotics.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), with the density of the densest packing known only in dimensions 1, 2, 3, 8, and 24; the remaining dimensions and the high-dimensional asymptotic behavior remain open.
solved_when: The densest-packing density is determined (with proof) in every dimension other than 1, 2, 3, 8, and 24, together with a characterization of its asymptotic behavior for high dimensions.

title: How many unit distances
open: How many pairs of points at unit distance can a set of n points in the Euclidean plane determine? More precisely, what is the true asymptotic growth, as a function of n, of the maximum number of unit distances among n planar points?
solved_when: Matching upper and lower bounds for the maximum number of unit distances determined by n points in the plane are established, determining its asymptotic order in n.

title: Borromean rings
open: Can three unknotted closed space curves that are not all circles always be arranged to form the Borromean rings? Formally, does there exist a triple of unknotted curves, not all three round circles, that cannot be positioned so as to realize the Borromean ring configuration?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), in the List of unsolved problems in mathematics (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: A specific triple of unknotted space curves, not all three circles, is exhibited together with a proof that no spatial placement of them forms the Borromean rings; or, conversely, it is proved that every such triple can be so arranged.

title: Dissection into orthoschemes
open: Can every simplex, in every dimension, be dissected into finitely many orthoschemes? More precisely, does an orthogonal dissection into orthoschemes exist for simplices of all dimensions (see Conjecture 23, p. 327)?
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07); see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics.
solved_when: A proof that simplices of every dimension admit a dissection into orthoschemes, or a counterexample exhibiting a dimension in which some simplex admits no such dissection.

title: Inscribed square problem
open: , also known as [[Toeplitz' conjecture]] and the square peg problem – does every [[Jordan curve]] have an inscribed square?

title: Moser's worm problem
open: What is the smallest possible area of a planar set that can cover (contain a congruent copy of) every unit-length curve in the plane? Equivalently, determine or tightly bound the minimal area of a universal cover for all unit "worms."
solved_when: The exact minimal area of such a universal covering set is determined, or matching upper and lower bounds are established.

title: Zarankiewicz problem
open: How many edges can a bipartite graph on a given number of vertices have while containing no complete bipartite subgraph of a given size? In other words, what is the maximum number of edges in a bipartite graph that avoids a specified complete bipartite subgraph?
solved_when: A sharp determination, or tight asymptotic bounds, on the maximum number of edges in a bipartite graph on n vertices with no complete bipartite subgraph of the given size, for general vertex counts and forbidden subgraph sizes.

title: Generalized star height problem
open: Can every regular language be described by a generalized regular expression whose nesting of Kleene stars is bounded? More precisely, is there a finite bound on the generalized star height of regular languages?
solved_when: A finite bound on the generalized star height of all regular languages is exhibited, or a family of regular languages of unbounded generalized star height is constructed.

title: Minimum overlap problem
open: How small can we make the maximum overlap when the set {1, …, 2n} is split into two sets of size n? Formally, for a partition into sets A and B with |A| = |B| = n, estimate the minimum possible value of the maximum number of times any integer appears as a termwise difference a − b with a ∈ A and b ∈ B.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (2026-10-07) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: An asymptotic estimate (up to constant factors, or better) is obtained for the minimum, over all partitions of {1, …, 2n} into two n-element sets A and B, of the maximum multiplicity of any value among the differences a − b.

title: Class number problem
open: are there infinitely many [[Class number problem#Real quadratic fields|real quadratic number fields]] with [[unique factorization]]?

title: Hilbert's 12th problem
open: extend the [[Kronecker–Weber theorem]] on [[Abelian extension]]s of \mathbb{Q} to any base number field

title: Woodin's
open: Does Ω-logic, in the presence of a proper class of Woodin cardinals, satisfy an analogue of Gödel's completeness theorem? Formally, this is the Ω-conjecture: assuming a proper class of Woodin cardinals, if a sentence is Ω-valid then it is Ω-provable.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics (checked 2026-10-07; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20mathematics).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the Ω-conjecture — that is, of the implication "if there is a proper class of Woodin cardinals, then Ω-logic satisfies an analogue of Gödel's completeness theorem" — is established.

title: Quadrisecant
open: Does every wild knot admit infinitely many quadrisecants? This is the conjectured extension of quadrisecant existence from tame to wild knots.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every wild knot has infinitely many quadrisecant lines is given.

title: Unknotting problem
open: Can it be decided in polynomial time whether a knot diagram represents the unknot? Formally, is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a knot diagram, determines whether the knot it depicts is the unknot?
solved_when: A polynomial-time algorithm for unknot recognition is given and its correctness proved — or, conversely, evidence that no such algorithm exists (e.g., a hardness separation) is established.
